title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the grain boundary resistance.

3. The moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the material is stored in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.
4. The moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 3, wherein the material has a true density of 1.8 g/cm3 to 5.5 g/cm3.
5. The moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more.
6. The moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the hydrolysis of the sulfide is suppressed such that the pH of water in contact with the powder remains 10 or less.
7. The moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 6, wherein the material is in the form of a powder, a pellet, or a sheet.

8. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer comprises the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1.
9. The solid-state lithium battery of claim 8, wherein the battery is pressed at a pressure of 1 MPa to 20 MPa during operation.
10. The solid-state lithium battery of claim 9, wherein the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal.
11. The solid-state lithium battery of claim 8, wherein the positive electrode layer comprises a lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide.
12. The solid-state lithium battery of claim 8, wherein the solid electrolyte layer has a thickness of 10 micrometers to 100 micrometers.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium zirconate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiNbO3 material. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more is described. The lithium secondary battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 80% or more. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLTO, LATP, and LLZO material. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. Part of the titanium in the NASICON-type LATP phase is substituted by germanium in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: An ion-conductive solid sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state battery including the sheet are described. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The roll temperature is 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 20 micrometers after calendering. An all-solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved interfacial resistance and a thinner electrolyte layer.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tantalum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The sintered body has a relative density of 94%, an average grain size of 5 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved high-voltage stability and sinterability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ion-conductive solid that does not require long mechanical milling. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the solid-state battery. Heat treatment at 550 degrees C after drying at 200 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved moisture stability.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 8 mol%. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. The disclosure is applicable to lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved electrochemical window.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ceramic ion conductor doped with gallium and sintered with LiF is described. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. Sintering at 1100 degrees C with a lithium excess of 8 mol% gives a relative density of 96% and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 60%. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 1.2 mS/cm. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. The SiS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the electrochemical window and cycle life.

Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. The SiS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the electrochemical window and cycle life.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid that remains stable up to 4.5 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The oxide particles have a core of the perovskite-type LLTO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in germanium. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. A capacity retention of 90% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. In a solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The widened electrochemical window improves the sinterability of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the cycle life.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. An H2S generation of 20 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using ethyl propionate
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt% or less. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C after drying at 150 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved moisture stability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and moisture stability.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using ethyl acetate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in ethyl acetate at 80 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The LLZO, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The solvent is ethyl acetate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a ceramic ion conductor with improved ionic conductivity and sinterability.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2WO4 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 15 nm. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability and cycle life.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor stable against oxidation above 5.2 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5.2 V. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved sinterability.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: A halide ion-conductive solid comprises a trigonal crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. In the trigonal structure, scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6. The median particle diameter D50 is 3 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 3 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the moisture stability at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-LiI glass. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite ion-conductive solid in which part of the bromine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-P2O5 glass. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. A solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Li3N layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a Li3N inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. The inorganic layer is formed by sputtering to a thickness of 120 nm to 600 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3YCl6 and beta-Li3PS4. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 300 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 1 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% over 100 cycles. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The bilayer structure improves the cycle life compared with a single inorganic layer.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for preparing the same
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The Li6PS5Cl and LLZO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ion-conductive solid film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The roll temperature is 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers after calendering. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. An all-solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved ionic conductivity and a thinner electrolyte layer.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by tin substitution is provided. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The substitution amount is 3 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.1 mS/cm or more. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 4.8 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The substitution amount is 10 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more and a conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm or more. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The oxide particles have a core of the phosphate-based NASICON phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in tin. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li7P3S11 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The content of Li2O is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.8 mS/cm or more. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The solid electrolyte shows improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li7P3S11 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The content of Li2O is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.8 mS/cm or more. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The solid electrolyte shows improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from ethyl acetate, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The ion-conductive solid obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt%. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives an ion-conductive solid with improved ionic conductivity and sinterability.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS and Li7P3S11 material. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 5.2 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The oxidation potential is 5.2 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 2 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the zirconium substitution and the surface region. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3, LLTO, and LLZO material. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 5.2 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The oxidation potential is 5.2 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 2 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the zirconium substitution and the surface region. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3, LLTO, and LLZO material. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The Li2ZrO3 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobium tantalum oxide, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The high coverage of the coating results in improved interfacial resistance at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery for lithium battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The average thickness of the coating is 2 nm to 10 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. The lithium tungstate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2WO4 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and nickel content of 80 mol% or more. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance and high-voltage stability.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3YCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium yttrium chloride formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6 material. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 15 nm. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life.

title: Gallium-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 15 mol%. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. Sintering is performed at 1100 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1100 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm and a relative density of 96%. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved high-voltage stability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobium tantalum oxide formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 3 nm. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobium tantalum oxide, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li3InCl6. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 10 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved grain boundary resistance and simpler handling.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase for lithium battery
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. A solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed bromine-iodine substitution
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.12 or less. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed bromine-iodine substitution
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.12 or less. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which a lithium fluoride-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the electronic conductivity of the solid electrolyte layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved dendrite suppression. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 1.5 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 300 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. The suppression of void formation improves the dendrite suppression during fast charging.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li7P3S11 phase and method for producing the same
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid shows improved cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A wet film of an ion-conductive solid cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The binder content of 2 wt% to 10 wt% gives a peel strength of 0.1 N/cm or more and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The wet film is dried at 80 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved sheet formability.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X solid electrolyte having anion disorder and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and LGPS material. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. An ionic conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.3 to 1.7. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The solid electrolyte provides improved electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 10 mol%. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1100 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm and a relative density of 95%. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Positive electrode active material having a double shell of lithium zirconate and lithium indium chloride for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for an all-solid-state battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid such as Li6PS5Cl includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide having 80 mol% or more of nickel among the transition metals, a first shell of lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) having an average thickness of 3 nm to 10 nm formed on the core particles, and a second shell of lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) having an average thickness of 10 nm to 40 nm formed on the first shell. The first shell is formed by a wet coating with a zirconium alkoxide solution and heat treatment at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and the second shell by ball milling the first-coated particles with Li3InCl6 powder at 100 rpm to 300 rpm under argon without damaging the core. The zirconate blocks the diffusion of transition metals and the formation of a space-charge layer, while the chloride, stable up to 4.3 V versus Li/Li+ with an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm, provides a low-resistance ion path to the sulfide. The coverage of the double shell measured by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 20 ohm cm2 or less. The active material widens the electrochemical window and improves the high-voltage stability.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure provides a Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Firing is performed at 480 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and electrochemical window.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a beta-Li3PS4 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing GeS2. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the moisture stability is improved.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The ion-conductive solid shows an ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 10 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the moisture stability and sinterability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS material. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The content of LiI is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.8 mS/cm or more. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The ion-conductive solid shows improved moisture stability and cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

2. The sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS material. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The content of LiI is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.8 mS/cm or more. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The ion-conductive solid shows improved moisture stability and cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by atomic layer deposition and lithium battery
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by atomic layer deposition followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% and no dendrite penetration is observed. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the grain boundary resistance and sinterability of the lithium metal battery.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a LiF inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. The LiF layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ceramic ion conductor. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The protective layer thickness is 40 nm to 200 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.8% or more. The bilayer structure improves the ionic conductivity and dendrite suppression compared with a single inorganic layer.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet solid electrolyte doped with tungsten and sintered with Al2O3 is described. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The dopant tungsten occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.15 to 0.5, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the moisture stability of the garnet layer.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of erbium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide ion-conductive solid in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3InCl6. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. In the monoclinic structure, erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The monoclinic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the ionic conductivity at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of erbium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide ion-conductive solid in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3InCl6. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. In the monoclinic structure, erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The monoclinic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the ionic conductivity at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure provides a Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-iodine substitution. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and LGPS material. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The material comprises Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. An ionic conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.1 to 0.55. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity and cycle life.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A precursor of the LLZO, Li2ZrO3, and LLTO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The oxide particles have a core of the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in germanium. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 75% or more. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved grain boundary resistance at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by solution casting. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and lithium fluoride (LiF). In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the dendrite suppression. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 300 cycles of stable plating and stripping. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 100 nm. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression and cycle life of the lithium metal battery.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and lithium battery
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 95% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The grain size is 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and the relative density is 92% or more after sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. Sintering is performed at 1200 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the interfacial resistance and cycle life.
