title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The precipitated thio-LISICON phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The solid electrolyte shows improved moisture stability and cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 5 mol%. Sintering is performed at 1100 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The sintered body has a relative density of 97%, an average grain size of 2 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved high-voltage stability and sinterability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using acetonitrile
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and Li7P3S11 material. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and electrochemical window.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte with trigonal structure and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF and Li3YCl6 material. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 200 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.6 micrometers to 6 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The oxidation stability limit is 4 V or more and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the electrochemical window and moisture stability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiTaO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and nickel content of 70 mol% or more. The lithium tantalate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the interfacial resistance and cycle life.

title: Slurry composition for a ceramic ion conductor layer using a nonpolar solvent and hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ceramic ion conductor particles are dispersed in heptane with a rubber binder and a dispersant. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The binder content is 3 wt%, the drying temperature is 120 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The Li3PS4 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4. A lithium secondary battery using the layer shows improved cycle life and a thin electrolyte layer.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a solid electrolyte with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.8 MPa or more. The resulting Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LLZO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the cycle life and interfacial resistance of the cell.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from ethyl propionate, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the sinterability.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of an ion-conductive solid is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 20 micrometers. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The LATP and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the ion-conductive solid, and the layer shows improved cycle life and sheet formability.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium scandium chloride solid electrolyte with orthorhombic structure
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. After dehydration under vacuum at 350 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and to a solid-state battery comprising the same. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The LGPS, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the solid-state battery. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A garnet solid electrolyte sintered body having an average grain size of 2 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The grain size is 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and the relative density is 92% or more after sintering at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The dopant niobium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.1 to 0.45, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the sinterability.

An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the sinterability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Firing is performed at 480 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobium tantalum oxide and to a method for producing the same. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The lithium niobium tantalum oxide shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant aluminum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.15 to 0.5, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1230 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm and a relative density of 97%. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a tin-rich surface region is described. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and LATP composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The tin substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. An all-solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The Li3PS4 and LGPS material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.075 or less. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 2.3 mS/cm. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The ion-conductive solid retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Aluminum-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with aluminum and sintered with Al2O3 is described. The disclosure is applicable to Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The sintered body has a relative density of 94%, an average grain size of 8 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. Sintering is performed at 1200 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLTO and LLZO material. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. After dehydration under vacuum at 300 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.

title: Slurry composition for an ion-conductive solid layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of an ion-conductive solid is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The binder content is 5 wt%, the drying temperature is 60 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ion-conductive solid does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved cycle life.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li7P3S11 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The LGPS and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.2 V. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3InCl6. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 200 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. Heat treatment at 200 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 0.56 mS/cm or more. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved high-voltage stability and rate capability.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNbO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A precursor of the Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 15 nm. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3InCl6 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved electrochemical window and interfacial resistance and rate capability.

title: Germanium-substituted NASICON-type LATP solid electrolyte stable above 4.5 V and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid electrolyte whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The Li2ZrO3 and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The oxide particles have a core of the NASICON-type LATP phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in germanium. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.5 V. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the lithium secondary battery. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The oxide solid electrolyte enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the high-voltage stability and sinterability.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium metal layer, an ion-conductive solid layer, and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The Li3YCl6, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The cell shows no short circuit for 200 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 20 MPa. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The suppression of void formation improves the cycle life during fast charging.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium metal layer, an ion-conductive solid layer, and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The Li3YCl6, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The cell shows no short circuit for 200 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 20 MPa. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The suppression of void formation improves the cycle life during fast charging.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by solution casting. The Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 100 nm. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% and no dendrite penetration is observed. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl material. The LiF layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the interfacial resistance of the lithium metal battery.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLZO, Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The solvent is a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a tin-rich surface region is described. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The tin substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 550 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.1 mS/cm or more. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the grain boundary resistance are improved.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a tin-rich surface region is described. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The tin substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 550 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.1 mS/cm or more. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the grain boundary resistance are improved.

title: Lithium borate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm is provided. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The Li3InCl6 and Li2ZrO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the grain boundary resistance and sinterability.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a solid electrolyte film without any solvent. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 100 degrees C to form a continuous film. The roll temperature is 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers after calendering. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The method shortens the process and improves the interfacial resistance of the layer.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium indium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction for lithium battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li3InCl6. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. The Li2ZrO3 and Li3InCl6 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The high coverage of the coating results in improved interfacial resistance at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a solid electrolyte with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.8 MPa or more. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. title: Hafnium-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ion-conductive solid stable above 5 V
abstract: Provided is a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ion-conductive solid in which hafnium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5 V. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. The LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved sinterability.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99% and no dendrite penetration is observed. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The LiF layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved ionic conductivity and Coulombic efficiency.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by oxygen substitution is provided. title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from 1,2-dimethoxyethane, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. The Li7P3S11 and LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C after drying at 180 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11 and LLZO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a solid electrolyte is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The wet film is dried at 60 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C has a thickness of 50 micrometers. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved cycle life and ionic conductivity.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide ceramic ion conductor precursor. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a ceramic ion conductor with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide solid electrolyte with an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more is described. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The resulting LLTO and Li2ZrO3 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The substitution amount is 10 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more and a conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm or more. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The widened electrochemical window improves the high-voltage stability of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 75% or more and an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm is provided. The LiNbO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the solid-state battery. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 4 cm3/g or less. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The silicon substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm and a retention of 85% after humid exposure. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 2 cm3/g. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The ceramic ion conductor retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved sinterability and moisture stability.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. A solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4, LLZO, and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state battery. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the sinterability.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 7.3 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte stable against oxidation above 5.2 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. A capacity retention of 88% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The oxide particles have a core of the phosphate-based NASICON phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The hafnium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the moisture stability and electrochemical window in contact with lithium.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 87% or more. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF) and beta-Li3PS4. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the cycle life is improved.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet comprises ion-conductive solid particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The binder content is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 2 MPa and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP, Li3PS4, and LLZO material. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved sheet formability and cycle life.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the solid electrolyte. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the lithium secondary battery. A Coulombic efficiency of 99% or more and a critical current density of 4 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The additive comprises indium in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved ionic conductivity and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium zirconate and to a method for producing the same. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiNbO3 material. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The ion-conductive component may be lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 40% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet comprises solid electrolyte particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. No solvent is used in the process, so the solid electrolyte does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The LATP, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. With a binder content of 1 wt% and a roll temperature of 120 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 30% or less. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved cycle life.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF). The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF material. In the orthorhombic structure, erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the solid-state battery. The halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.3 V versus Li/Li+. The titanium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a tin-rich surface region is described. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 2 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. Specific examples are Li7P3S11 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the sinterability.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and to a lithium secondary battery comprising the same. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 550 degrees C. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. When fired at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 2.6 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life and ionic conductivity.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and to a lithium secondary battery comprising the same. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 550 degrees C. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. When fired at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 2.6 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life and ionic conductivity.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into an ion-conductive solid layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 200 nm. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 500 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the solid-state battery. The inorganic layer is formed by sputtering to a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved dendrite suppression.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in ethyl acetate to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. Specific examples are Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the all-solid-state battery. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability and moisture stability.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa with a zinc additive. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 and Li3PS4 material. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li3YCl6 and beta-Li3PS4. A stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. The critical current density is 0.7 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the ionic conductivity of the solid-state cell.
