title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with tungsten and sintered with Li2CO3 is described. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The dopant tungsten occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. When v is 0.4, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved electrochemical window.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with tungsten and sintered with Li2CO3 is described. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The dopant tungsten occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. When v is 0.4, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved electrochemical window.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the ionic conductivity at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in ethyl propionate at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid tin binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The resulting Li7P3S11 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li7P3S11 phase and production method thereof
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 70%. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobium tantalum oxide formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The lithium niobium tantalum oxide shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 150 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite solid electrolyte having anion disorder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The Li7P3S11 and LGPS material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 550 degrees C. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3YCl6 shell with high coverage and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium yttrium chloride formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3InCl6. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium chloride ceramic ion conductor prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. A precursor of the Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.6 micrometers to 6 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. In the orthorhombic structure, yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.02 to 0.25. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved moisture stability and rate capability.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a NASICON-type LATP solid electrolyte in which germanium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. A capacity retention of 92% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved sinterability.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide solid electrolyte with an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more is described. The oxide particles have a core of the perovskite-type LLTO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in tin. With tin substitution of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Part of the titanium in the perovskite-type LLTO phase is substituted by tin in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LATP, LLTO, and LLZO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved sinterability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3BO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 80 mol% or more. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Lithium phosphorus oxynitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF and Li3YCl6 material. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% and no dendrite penetration is observed. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the interfacial resistance.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid that remains stable up to 5.2 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 88%. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. Part of the titanium in the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase is substituted by tin in an amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the sheet formability of the electrolyte layer.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a solid electrolyte film without any solvent. A sheet of 20 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP material. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved interfacial resistance and sheet formability.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer that has a solid content of 50 wt% to 70 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. The LLZO, LATP, and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The slurry has a solid content of 50 wt% to 70 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The binder content of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% gives a peel strength of 0.1 N/cm or more and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the ceramic ion conductor, and the layer shows improved ionic conductivity and cycle life.

title: Slurry composition for an ion-conductive solid layer using a nonpolar solvent and polyisobutylene
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ion-conductive solid particles are dispersed in butyl butyrate with a rubber binder and a dispersant. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO, LATP, and Li6PS5Cl material. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The solid content is 50 wt% to 70 wt%, the viscosity is 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C in an oven. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and method for preparing the same
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 2 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1230 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a relative density of 94%. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the sinterability is improved.

13. title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-P2O5 glass. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity.

title: Lithium phosphorus oxynitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF). After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% and no dendrite penetration is observed. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The inorganic layer is formed by sputtering to a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved ionic conductivity and cycle life.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tungstate and to a method for producing the same. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the moisture stability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. A precursor of the Li2ZrO3 and LATP material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 8 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 30%. The high coverage of the coating results in improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. A residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the ionic conductivity of the product.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a solid electrolyte with improved sinterability.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium scandium chloride ion-conductive solid with orthorhombic structure and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ion-conductive solid in which zirconium is substituted for part of the scandium in a lithium scandium chloride framework. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 250 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. In the orthorhombic structure, scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. After dehydration under vacuum at 250 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. A solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the moisture stability and electrochemical window.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 5.1 mS/cm. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.12 or less. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved moisture stability compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li7P3S11 phase and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li7P3S11 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing P2O5. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LGPS material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The content of P2O5 is 5 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved electrochemical window and rate performance.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure provides a Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the moisture stability of the material is retained after storage.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 1.4 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. A Coulombic efficiency of 98.8% or more and a critical current density of 2 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved ionic conductivity and dendrite suppression.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa with a magnesium additive. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 3 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 500 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved dendrite suppression. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF). Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the dendrite suppression is improved.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Al2O3 layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ion-conductive solid. The Al2O3 layer of 300 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 300 nm. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state battery. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the ion-conductive solid at the negative electrode is suppressed and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an arsenic-free antimony-rich surface region is described. The Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state lithium battery. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 20 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the grain boundary resistance and sinterability.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The solvent is acetonitrile, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C after drying at 150 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a ceramic ion conductor with improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.

abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The solvent is acetonitrile, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C after drying at 150 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a ceramic ion conductor with improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ceramic ion conductor. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 300 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The inorganic layer is formed by atomic layer deposition to a thickness of 200 nm to 1000 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the lithium secondary battery. The bilayer structure improves the interfacial resistance compared with a single inorganic layer.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, Li2ZrO3, and LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and lithium battery
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by tin substitution is provided. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.6 mS/cm or more. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The LLZO and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved moisture stability.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ceramic ion conductor. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and beta-Li3PS4, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The LiF and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF) and beta-Li3PS4. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. A solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobium tantalum oxide, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiNbO3 and Li6PS5Cl material. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Dendrite-suppressing zinc additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and method for preparing the same
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. With the additive in an amount of 5 wt% and a stack pressure of 10 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99%. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The LATP and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved cycle life and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the ionic conductivity of the product.

title: Niobium-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant niobium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The sintered body has a relative density of 97%, an average grain size of 2 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The dopant niobium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.35 to 0.7, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. Examples of the ion conductor include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The densification improves the mechanical strength and the high-voltage stability of the garnet layer.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. With zirconium substitution of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and a porosity of 20% or less is provided. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. With a binder content of 2 wt% and a roll temperature of 100 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 20% or less. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved sheet formability and interfacial resistance.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 92% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The total ionic conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Lithium nitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by sputtering. The Li3N layer of 200 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. A solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved cycle life and ionic conductivity.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved sinterability.

4. The method of claim 1, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 4.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved sinterability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2ZrO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and rate capability.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a solid electrolyte sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LATP, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The binder content is 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 2 MPa and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the ionic conductivity and sheet formability.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide solid electrolyte whose decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The ion-conductive component may be Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more and a conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm or more. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage and method for preparing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state lithium battery is described. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The Li2ZrO3 and Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li3InCl6. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and rate capability.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide solid electrolyte that does not require long mechanical milling. Specific examples are Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt%. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The resulting Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium scandium bromide solid electrolyte with orthorhombic structure for lithium battery
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises an orthorhombic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Br6. In an embodiment the material is Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.6 micrometers to 6 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder for lithium battery
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the cycle life.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor stable against oxidation above 5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5 V. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises a monoclinic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3YCl6. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 material. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The Li3YCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The median particle diameter D50 is 1 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises a monoclinic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3YCl6. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 material. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The Li3YCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The median particle diameter D50 is 1 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.

title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y) and to a solid-state battery comprising the same. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and moisture stability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The glass phase contains GeS2 in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. A precursor of the Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. A halide coating is compatible with the solid electrolyte because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The content of GeS2 is 3 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.8 mS/cm or more. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The solid electrolyte shows improved electrochemical window and cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium erbium chloride ion-conductive solid with trigonal structure and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of erbium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.3 V. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF). Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better moisture stability.
