title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on NASICON-type LATP and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 80%. Part of the titanium in the NASICON-type LATP phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The positive electrode active material is a 5 V spinel, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The low electronic conductivity of the LLTO material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the grain boundary resistance and sinterability of the electrolyte layer.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid in which part of the bromine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. An ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.1 to 1.5. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. The ion-conductive solid provides improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid in which part of the bromine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. An ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.1 to 1.5. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. The ion-conductive solid provides improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.

title: Dendrite-suppressing magnesium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ion-conductive solid. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the electronic conductivity of the ion-conductive solid layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. A stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The Li6PS5Cl material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The critical current density is 1 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 250 cycles or more. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The method prevents short circuit and improves the cycle life without a thick protective layer.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using an indium-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium metal layer, an ion-conductive solid layer, and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. With the additive in an amount of 5 wt% and a stack pressure of 20 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99%. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The LiNbO3, Li3InCl6, and Li2ZrO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The disclosure is applicable to lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The high coverage of the coating results in improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tantalate and to a method for producing the same. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 10 nm. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using 1,2-dimethoxyethane
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ion-conductive solid that does not require long mechanical milling. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives an ion-conductive solid with improved sinterability.

title: Dendrite-suppressing indium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The indium additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. With the additive in an amount of 0.5 wt% and a stack pressure of 2 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.7%. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved electrochemical window and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in ethyl propionate at 80 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 4.1 mS/cm. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the ionic conductivity of the product.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for an all-solid-state lithium battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Specific examples are Li7P3S11. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 9.6 mS/cm. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a silver-containing additive layer
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa with a silver additive. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3YCl6, LLZO, and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% or more and a critical current density of 1.5 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The reaction at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X solid electrolyte having anion disorder and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.15 or less. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The mixed halogen substitution improves the ionic conductivity of the lithium secondary battery.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: An argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. An ionic conductivity of 2.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.2 to 1.6. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life and moisture stability.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite ceramic ion conductor in which part of the bromine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the lithium secondary battery. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 8 mol%. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. Sintering at 1100 degrees C with a lithium excess of 8 mol% gives a relative density of 94% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4. The Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ion-conductive solid whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4. The Li3PS4 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ion-conductive solid provides improved moisture stability compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.

abstract: A Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.075 or less. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity and cycle life.

title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.075 or less. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity and cycle life.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tantalate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6. The average thickness of the coating is 2 nm to 10 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and cycle life and rate capability.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a zinc-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 2.1 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. With the additive in an amount of 0.5 wt% and a stack pressure of 5 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.3%. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The additive comprises zinc in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The zinc additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li7P3S11, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The method prevents short circuit and improves the grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity without a thick protective layer.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet comprises ceramic ion conductor particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. With a binder content of 1 wt% and a roll temperature of 60 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 16% or less. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. No solvent is used in the process, so the ceramic ion conductor does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the interfacial resistance of the cell.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based lithium secondary battery is described. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 15 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based lithium secondary battery is described. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 15 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity and rate capability.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte with orthorhombic structure and production method thereof
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. When z is 0.4, the conductivity is 3 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 and LiF material. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the electrochemical window at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 20 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The ceramic ion conductor retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a zinc-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 1.4 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% or more and a critical current density of 2 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The suppression of void formation improves the interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity during fast charging.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ceramic ion conductor. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The Li3YCl6, LLZO, and LiF material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99% after 100 cycles. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF). A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The inorganic layer is formed by atomic layer deposition to a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression of the lithium metal battery.

6. The method of claim 5, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.

8. The all-solid-state battery of claim 7, wherein the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y). The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the cycle life.

title: Lithium indium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 75% or more and an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm is provided. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 10 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The magnesium additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5% after 100 cycles. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. In a solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The material comprises Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and the electronic conductivity of the solid electrolyte layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved moisture stability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The halide is applied to the positive electrode active material by a wet coating with an alkoxide-free solution, giving a coated cathode. Specific examples are Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide solid electrolyte with an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more is described. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state battery. The LLZO and LLTO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.8 V. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. Part of the titanium in the NASICON-type LATP phase is substituted by germanium in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The widened electrochemical window improves the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobium tantalum oxide and to a method for producing the same. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Specific examples are lithium niobate (LiNbO3), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and iodine. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 4.8 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 80%. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The hafnium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the sinterability and high-voltage stability in contact with lithium.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the germanium substitution and the surface region. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The oxide particles have a core of the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in germanium. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. When fired at 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which magnesium is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% to suppress dendrites. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99% after 100 cycles. The magnesium additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which titanium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium chloride framework. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and Li3InCl6. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The LiF, Li3YCl6, and Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the solid-state battery without a drying step. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. title: Dendrite-suppressing lithium fluoride additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa with a lithium fluoride additive. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The additive content is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, the stack pressure is 10 MPa to 40 MPa, and the critical current density is 3 mA/cm2. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6, beta-Li3PS4, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The Li3YCl6, Li3PS4, and LiF material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the cycle life.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6 and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 10 nm. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The lithium niobium tantalum oxide shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the high-voltage stability and cycle life.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The solvent is ethyl propionate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a solid electrolyte with improved sinterability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobium tantalum oxide and to a method for producing the same. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The material comprises Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobium tantalum oxide, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from 1,2-dimethoxyethane, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The suspension concentration is 10 wt%, the reaction temperature is 40 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 200 degrees C. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. After drying, the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability and moisture stability.

3. The method of claim 1, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 430 degrees C to 480 degrees C.
4. The method of claim 1, wherein the reaction temperature is 35 degrees C to 50 degrees C.
5. The method of claim 1, wherein the suspension further contains LiCl dissolved therein.
6. The method of claim 1, wherein the precipitate is separated by filtration before the removing of the solvent.
7. A solid electrolyte produced by the method of claim 1.
8. The solid electrolyte of claim 7, wherein the material is in the form of particles having a BET specific surface area of 1 m2/g to 20 m2/g.

9. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer comprises the solid electrolyte of claim 7.
10. The all-solid-state battery of claim 9, wherein the positive electrode layer further comprises a conductive carbon in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt%.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from 1,2-dimethoxyethane, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The suspension concentration is 10 wt%, the reaction temperature is 40 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 200 degrees C. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. After drying, the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability and moisture stability.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in tetrahydrofuran at 40 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state battery without a drying step. The solvent is tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved sinterability.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ion-conductive solid whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the lithium secondary battery. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 5.1 mS/cm. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 550 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.
claims: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 680 degrees C.
2. The sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the crystal phase is superionic with an activation energy of 0.30 eV or less.
3. The sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the material is in the form of a powder, a pellet, or a sheet.
4. The sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein a particle size distribution of the material has a D90 of 20 micrometers or less.
5. The sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein 1.5 <= a <= 1.7.

6. A method for producing the sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, LiCl, and LiBr at a molar ratio corresponding to the composition to obtain a precursor mixture; mechanically milling the precursor mixture; and firing the milled mixture at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an inert gas atmosphere.
7. The method of claim 6, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.
8. The method of claim 6, further comprising pulverizing the product to a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers.

9. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer comprises the sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1.
10. The lithium secondary battery of claim 9, wherein the battery is pressed at a pressure of 1 MPa to 20 MPa during operation.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 60% or more are obtained. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 5 cm3/g. The electrode mixture of the solid-state lithium battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Hafnium-substituted phosphate-based NASICON ion-conductive solid stable above 4.8 V and production method thereof
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 4.8 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 83% or more. Suitable compositions include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state battery. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved grain boundary resistance and sinterability.

5. The solid-state battery of claim 4, wherein the ion-conductive solid layer has a thickness of 10 micrometers to 100 micrometers.
6. The solid-state battery of claim 4, wherein the positive electrode layer comprises a lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite solid electrolyte having anion disorder and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 550 degrees C. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. An ionic conductivity of 2.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.4 to 0.85. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The solid electrolyte provides improved ionic conductivity and cycle life compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed bromine-iodine substitution
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and to a lithium secondary battery comprising the same. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 3.5 mS/cm. The ion-conductive solid provides improved cycle life compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and lithium battery
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by arsenic-free antimony substitution is provided. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 1 hours. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 20 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A solid-state lithium battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved interfacial resistance.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm and a retention of 85% after humid exposure. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and LLZO material. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. A solid-state lithium battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sinterability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobium tantalum oxide formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 3 nm. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The lithium niobium tantalum oxide shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. With germanium substitution of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The widened electrochemical window improves the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by sputtering followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 100 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 2 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99% over 100 cycles. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3YCl6. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The Al2O3 layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the interfacial resistance.

title: Lithium nitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The material comprises Li3YCl6, beta-Li3PS4, and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The protective layer thickness is 20 nm to 100 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.3% or more. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression and ionic conductivity of the lithium metal battery.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which lithium fluoride is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% to suppress dendrites. A Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% or more and a critical current density of 4 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. The lithium fluoride additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved cycle life and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from tetrahydrofuran, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved sinterability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobium tantalum oxide and to a method for producing the same. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The coating layer has an average thickness of 3 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the solid-state battery. The high coverage of the coating results in improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
