title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a solid electrolyte with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.8 MPa or more. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The tensile strength is 1.8 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The LLZO and LATP material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. A lithium secondary battery using the sheet shows improved cycle life and a thinner electrolyte layer.

11. The method of claim 10, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte with monoclinic structure and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide solid electrolyte in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The resulting LiF material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The monoclinic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 250 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF). The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium scandium bromide ion-conductive solid with monoclinic structure and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of scandium and zirconium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.5 V. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The oxidation stability limit is 4.3 V or more and the conductivity is 0.56 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF). The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the ionic conductivity.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 80%. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the ionic conductivity of the electrolyte layer.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid in which part of the bromine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. A precursor of the LGPS, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 4.2 mS/cm. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and moisture stability.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte with monoclinic structure and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and titanium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.5 V. Suitable compositions include lithium fluoride (LiF). An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. In the monoclinic structure, yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.3 micrometers to 3 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.3 to 0.55. The LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-P2O5 glass. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 and LGPS material. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. Specific examples are argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the cycle life.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-LiI glass. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LGPS and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 30% to 65% by X-ray diffraction. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li7P3S11, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved ionic conductivity compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 4 cm3/g or less. An H2S generation of 4 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 2 cm3/g. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite solid electrolyte having anion disorder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The resulting Li6PS5Cl material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.12 or less. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and ionic conductivity.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of indium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide solid electrolyte in which indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.1 to 0.35. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The halide is applied to the positive electrode active material by a wet coating with an alkoxide-free solution, giving a coated cathode. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material comprises Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the moisture stability at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of indium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide solid electrolyte in which indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.1 to 0.35. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The halide is applied to the positive electrode active material by a wet coating with an alkoxide-free solution, giving a coated cathode. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material comprises Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the moisture stability at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y) and to a lithium secondary battery comprising the same. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm and a retention of 70% after humid exposure. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the ionic conductivity.

title: Tin-substituted titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ion-conductive solid stable above 4.8 V and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ion-conductive solid. The substitution amount is 10 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more and a conductivity of 0.21 mS/cm or more. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3InCl6. The Li6PS5Cl, Li2ZrO3, and Li3InCl6 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The coating layer has an average thickness of 8 nm and a coverage of 80%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, Li2ZrO3, and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The binder content of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% gives a peel strength of 0.1 N/cm or more and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the solid electrolyte, and the layer shows improved sheet formability and interfacial resistance.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and lithium battery
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by silicon substitution is provided. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. After exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours, the conductivity retention is 90%. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. An all-solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2ZrO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The disclosure is applicable to Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLTO material. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for preparing the same
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. An H2S generation of 20 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 70% or more are obtained. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved sinterability.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a magnesium-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium metal layer, an ion-conductive solid layer, and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. With the additive in an amount of 0.5 wt% and a stack pressure of 2 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5%. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The Li3YCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The method prevents short circuit and improves the dendrite suppression and ionic conductivity without a thick protective layer.

title: Self-supporting ceramic ion conductor sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and a lithium secondary battery including the sheet are described. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. With a binder content of 0.5 wt% and a roll temperature of 80 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 20% or less. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. No solvent is used in the process, so the ceramic ion conductor does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. The method shortens the process and improves the cycle life and interfacial resistance of the layer.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 10 cm3/g or less. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm and a retention of 70% after humid exposure. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the moisture stability are improved.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium zirconate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 5 nm. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window.

A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 35% or more.

3. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

5. The positive electrode active material of claim 4, wherein the coating layer comprises at least one selected from the group consisting of LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, LiTaO3, Li2WO4, Li3BO3, and Li3InCl6.
6. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 104% or more.
7. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.
8. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the material has a true density of 1.8 g/cm3 to 5.5 g/cm3.

9. A method for producing the positive electrode active material of claim 1, the method comprising: preparing a coating solution containing a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate; applying the coating solution to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed; and heat-treating the coated core particles at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere.
10. The method of claim 9, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.
11. The method of claim 10, wherein the mixing is performed in a planetary mixer for 10 minutes to 120 minutes.
12. The method of claim 11, wherein the inert gas atmosphere is argon or nitrogen.

13. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the positive electrode layer comprises the positive electrode active material of claim 1.
14. The solid-state battery of claim 13, wherein the ceramic ion conductor layer has a thickness of 10 micrometers to 100 micrometers.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming an ion-conductive solid sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. The sheet has a thickness of 30 micrometers, a porosity of 5%, a tensile strength of 3 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved grain boundary resistance.

6. The free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet of claim 1, wherein the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm.
7. The free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet of claim 1, further comprising a binder in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt%.
8. The free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet of claim 7, wherein the material has a water content of 0.5 wt% or less as measured by Karl Fischer titration.
9. The free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet of claim 1, wherein the material is substantially free of a liquid component.
10. The free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet of claim 1, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 21 micrometers to 45 micrometers.
11. The free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet of claim 1, wherein the material is stored in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.

title: Lithium indium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The coating layer has an average thickness of 3 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. The material comprises Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF). The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The Li2O addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid arsenic-free antimony binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 4.5 mS/cm. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the grain boundary resistance and sinterability.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid arsenic-free antimony binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 4.5 mS/cm. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the grain boundary resistance and sinterability.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of scandium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide solid electrolyte of scandium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.5 V. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. In the orthorhombic structure, scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 3 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved moisture stability and rate capability.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 200 nm to 1000 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 and LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The inorganic layer is formed by atomic layer deposition to a thickness of 200 nm to 1000 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved sinterability and high-voltage stability.

7. The solid-state lithium battery of claim 5, wherein the positive electrode layer comprises a lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in 1,2-dimethoxyethane at 25 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved moisture stability.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved moisture stability.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 70%. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved moisture stability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 7.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.

title: Tin-substituted perovskite-type LLTO ion-conductive solid stable above 5 V and method for producing the same
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid that remains stable up to 5 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5 V. The low electronic conductivity of the Li6PS5Cl material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the moisture stability is improved.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer. The binder is styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane. The slurry has a solid content of 50 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 15 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved cycle life.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life and ionic conductivity.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 material. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and nickel content of 50 mol% or more. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life.

title: Lithium phosphorus oxynitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li3YCl6. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 300 cycles of stable plating and stripping. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a silicon-rich surface region is described. A solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 2 hours. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The silicon substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the solid-state battery. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved ionic conductivity and sinterability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium indium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3InCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state lithium battery. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. The high coverage of the coating results in improved interfacial resistance at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Wet coating method for forming a solid electrolyte layer on a release film and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A wet film of a solid electrolyte cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. The binder content is 1 wt%, the drying temperature is 60 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The wet film is dried at 60 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the cycle life of the cell.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ion-conductive solid comprises a monoclinic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. When z is 0.1, the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. In the monoclinic structure, erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state lithium battery. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the electrochemical window at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiPON layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. The LiPON layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ceramic ion conductor. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved dendrite suppression. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved dendrite suppression.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The electrode mixture of the solid-state lithium battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. Heat treatment at 550 degrees C after drying at 150 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. In a solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the moisture stability of the product.

title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for an all-solid-state battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y). When fired at 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The Li7P3S11 and LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.

title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for an all-solid-state battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y). When fired at 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The Li7P3S11 and LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The coating layer has an average thickness of 3 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. The resulting Li3InCl6 and LiNbO3 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into an ion-conductive solid layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF). A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 500 cycles of stable plating and stripping. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiF material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The bilayer structure improves the cycle life compared with a single inorganic layer.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium metal layer, an ion-conductive solid layer, and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 4 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 500 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The suppression of void formation improves the ionic conductivity during fast charging.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a Li7P3S11 phase and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li7P3S11 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 3.1 mS/cm. A solid-state battery comprising the LGPS, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The GeS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium indium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance and cycle life.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium indium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance and cycle life.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution for lithium battery
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. When fired at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 7.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The Li7P3S11 and LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better moisture stability.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ion-conductive solid comprises a trigonal crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, InCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 1.47 mS/cm or more. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) disposed on the surface of the core particles. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The LiNbO3 and Li3InCl6 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 8 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 3.5 mS/cm. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 2.5 mS/cm. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The solid electrolyte shows improved electrochemical window and moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
