title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the lithium secondary battery. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The average thickness of the coating is 6 nm to 30 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The lithium borate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the sinterability and moisture stability.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more and a conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm or more. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The oxide ceramic ion conductor enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the moisture stability.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more and a conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm or more. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The oxide ceramic ion conductor enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the moisture stability.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. When fired at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. Specific examples are argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability.

title: Aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the cycle life.

title: Slurry composition for a solid electrolyte layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-butadiene rubber
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming a solid electrolyte layer. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The ion-conductive component may be Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 30 micrometers. The LGPS, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The LGPS, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved electrochemical window.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiTaO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 50% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Br6 and lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Br6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The monoclinic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. In the monoclinic structure, erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. The halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.5 V versus Li/Li+. The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the moisture stability and high-voltage stability.

title: Wet coating method for forming a solid electrolyte layer on a release film and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The binder is styrene-butadiene rubber in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The solid content is 40 wt% to 60 wt%, the viscosity is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved interfacial resistance.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the ionic conductivity is retained.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. Heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives an orthorhombic phase with a conductivity of 0.84 mS/cm or more. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and LiF material. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the electrochemical window at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for preparing the same
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor that remains stable up to 4.5 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLTO and Li2ZrO3 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 92%. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and production method thereof
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 90% or more and an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm is provided. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 10 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 30%. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6 and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and interfacial resistance.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and method for producing the same
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. The LGPS and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The ion-conductive solid shows improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ceramic ion conductor layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state battery without a drying step. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). When fired at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 2.6 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. When fired at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.12 or less. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for a lithium secondary battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The ion-conductive solid provides improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li7P3S11 phase and lithium battery
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 40% to 75% by X-ray diffraction. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The protective layer thickness is 200 nm to 1000 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.8% or more. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the interfacial resistance and electrochemical window of the lithium metal battery.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved grain boundary resistance and moisture stability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 60%. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 320 degrees C. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The solid electrolyte shows improved electrochemical window compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li7P3S11. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and production method thereof
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm and a retention of 70% after humid exposure. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the grain boundary resistance.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which titanium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium chloride framework. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A precursor of the Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The material comprises Li3YCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. After dehydration under vacuum at 350 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3InCl6 shell with high coverage and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 75% or more and an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm is provided. The average thickness of the coating is 6 nm to 30 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The Li6PS5Cl and LiNbO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium indium chloride, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium chloride ion-conductive solid prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3InCl6. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The oxidation stability limit is 4.3 V or more and the conductivity is 1.47 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The material comprises Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3InCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the moisture stability at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Dendrite-suppressing zinc additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ceramic ion conductor. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A precursor of the LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The additive content is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, the stack pressure is 5 MPa to 20 MPa, and the critical current density is 1.5 mA/cm2. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved dendrite suppression.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li7P3S11. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The tin substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. A precursor of the LLZO and Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the moisture stability are improved.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using acetonitrile
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in acetonitrile to give a sulfide ceramic ion conductor precursor. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 4.1 mS/cm. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the ionic conductivity of the product.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-GeS2 glass. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 2.5 mS/cm. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3BO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. A solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and electrochemical window and rate capability.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer that has a solid content of 40 wt% to 60 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s. The wet film is dried at 60 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The binder is styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The method further comprises a synthesis step in which a solvate complex is precipitated and heat-treated to obtain the powder. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The solid content is 40 wt% to 60 wt%, the viscosity is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. A solid-state battery using the layer shows improved sheet formability and a thin electrolyte layer.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer that has a solid content of 40 wt% to 60 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s. The wet film is dried at 60 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The binder is styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The method further comprises a synthesis step in which a solvate complex is precipitated and heat-treated to obtain the powder. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The solid content is 40 wt% to 60 wt%, the viscosity is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. A solid-state battery using the layer shows improved sheet formability and a thin electrolyte layer.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 8 mol%. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1200 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm and a relative density of 95%. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. Sintering is performed at 1200 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3YCl6 shell with high coverage
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium yttrium chloride formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium yttrium chloride, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li3InCl6, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The Li2ZrO3, Li3InCl6, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life.

title: Ceramic ion conductor slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer comprises ceramic ion conductor particles, a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The binder is hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent heptane. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The solid content is 50 wt% to 70 wt%, the viscosity is 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a ceramic ion conductor layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% after 100 cycles. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 500 nm. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The Ag-C layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ceramic ion conductor. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy for lithium battery
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and iodine. The LLZO and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. When fired at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and moisture stability.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ion-conductive solid with an oxidation limit of 4.7 V or more is described. With zirconium substitution of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The oxide particles have a core of the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in zirconium. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability of the electrolyte layer.

title: Wet coating method for forming a solid electrolyte layer on a release film and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A wet film of a solid electrolyte cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The solid content is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, the viscosity is 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The wet film is dried at 120 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the solid electrolyte, and the layer shows improved cycle life and ionic conductivity.

title: Wet coating method for forming a solid electrolyte layer on a release film and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A wet film of a solid electrolyte cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The solid content is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, the viscosity is 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The wet film is dried at 120 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the solid electrolyte, and the layer shows improved cycle life and ionic conductivity.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which indium is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% to suppress dendrites. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The cell shows no short circuit for 500 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 2 MPa. The LiF and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the interfacial resistance of the solid-state cell.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6 and method for producing the same
abstract: A halide ceramic ion conductor comprises a monoclinic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ceramic ion conductor layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state battery without a drying step. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The oxidation stability limit is 4.1 V or more and the conductivity is 0.56 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. In the monoclinic structure, yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the high-voltage stability at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. An ionic conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.1 to 1.5. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Li3N layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ceramic ion conductor. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), beta-Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the lithium secondary battery. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 500 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A precursor of the LiF, Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the ceramic ion conductor at the negative electrode is suppressed and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.1, and the room-temperature conductivity is 8.5 mS/cm. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life and moisture stability of the all-solid-state lithium battery.

The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life and moisture stability of the all-solid-state lithium battery.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Al2O3 layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ceramic ion conductor. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li3YCl6, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 200 cycles of stable plating and stripping. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved cycle life.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 60% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.6 mS/cm or more. The Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the interfacial resistance.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an ion-conductive solid whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state battery. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 87% or more. Part of the titanium in the titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase is substituted by germanium in an amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the germanium substitution and the surface region. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The widened electrochemical window improves the sinterability of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a thio-LISICON phase for lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and Li6PS5Cl material. The content of LiI is 2 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.8 mS/cm or more. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life and interfacial resistance.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a silicon-rich surface region is described. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. After exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity retention is 85%. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the moisture stability are improved.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a thio-LISICON phase and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-SiS2 glass. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the moisture stability of the cell.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li7P3S11 phase for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li7P3S11 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. After heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.8 mS/cm. The Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The material comprises Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from ethyl acetate, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state lithium battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. The resulting Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved ionic conductivity and sinterability.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from ethyl acetate, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state lithium battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. The resulting Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved ionic conductivity and sinterability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium zirconate and to a method for producing the same. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The material comprises Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life and interfacial resistance.

3. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the material is in the form of a powder, a pellet, or a sheet.
4. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the material has a true density of 1.8 g/cm3 to 5.5 g/cm3.
5. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more.
6. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the coating layer is amorphous as confirmed by transmission electron microscopy.
7. The positive electrode active material of claim 6, wherein a lithium ion transference number of the material is 0.99 or more.
8. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 95% or more.
9. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the material has an activation energy for lithium ion conduction of 0.40 eV or less.
10. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide is suppressed.
11. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the material is substantially free of a liquid component.
12. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein a content of carbon in the material is 0.5 wt% or less.
13. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, further comprising a binder in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt%.
14. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 320 degrees C.
15. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 33% or more.
16. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 1.5 micrometers to 15 micrometers.

17. A method for producing the positive electrode active material of claim 1, the method comprising: preparing a coating solution containing a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate; applying the coating solution to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed; and heat-treating the coated core particles at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere.
18. The method of claim 17, wherein the inert gas atmosphere is argon or nitrogen.
19. The method of claim 17, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.
20. The method of claim 17, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.

21. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the positive electrode layer comprises the positive electrode active material of claim 1.
22. The all-solid-state lithium battery of claim 21, further comprising an intermediate layer disposed between the negative electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer.
23. The all-solid-state lithium battery of claim 21, wherein the positive electrode layer comprises a lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide.
24. The all-solid-state lithium battery of claim 21, wherein the battery is pressed at a pressure of 1 MPa to 20 MPa during operation.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiTaO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises a trigonal crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 0.56 mS/cm or more. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better high-voltage stability.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises a trigonal crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 0.56 mS/cm or more. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better high-voltage stability.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and method for preparing the same
abstract: A halide ceramic ion conductor comprises a monoclinic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6 material. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. After dehydration under vacuum at 300 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. In the monoclinic structure, erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a ceramic ion conductor is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The binder is polyisobutylene in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent anisole. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C has a thickness of 30 micrometers. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C in an oven. The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the interfacial resistance of the layer.
