2. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 60% or more.
3. The positive electrode active material of claim 2, wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 66% or more.
4. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 94 mol% or more.
5. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm.
6. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 1.2 micrometers to 4 micrometers.
7. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the coating layer comprises at least one selected from the group consisting of LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, LiTaO3, Li2WO4, Li3BO3, and Li3InCl6.
8. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.
9. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein an electronic conductivity of the material at 25 degrees C is 1 x 10^-8 S/cm or less.

10. A method for producing the positive electrode active material of claim 1, the method comprising: preparing a coating solution containing a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobium tantalum oxide; applying the coating solution to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed; and heat-treating the coated core particles at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere.
11. The method of claim 10, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.
12. The method of claim 10, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.

13. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the positive electrode layer comprises the positive electrode active material of claim 1.
14. The all-solid-state lithium battery of claim 13, wherein the battery is pressed at a pressure of 1 MPa to 20 MPa during operation.
15. The all-solid-state lithium battery of claim 14, wherein the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Described is an oxide solid electrolyte whose decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLTO, LLZO, and Li2ZrO3 material. The disclosure is applicable to Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The oxidation potential is 5.2 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 5 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance of the electrolyte layer.
claims: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 25 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 73% or more.
2. The oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein an anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles has a thickness of 10 nm or less.
3. The oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 3 mol%.
4. The oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the material is substantially free of a liquid component.
5. The oxide solid electrolyte of claim 4, wherein the surface region comprises lithium phosphate.
6. The oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein an electronic conductivity of the material at 25 degrees C is 1 x 10^-8 S/cm or less.
7. The oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 0.45 micrometers to 4.5 micrometers.
8. The oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.27 mS/cm or more.
9. The oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 88% or more.
10. The oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the substituting element is at least one selected from the group consisting of Ge, Zr, Hf, and Sn.
11. The oxide solid electrolyte of claim 3, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 1.9 mol% to 2.7 mol%.
12. The oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

13. A method for producing the oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing lithium, titanium, hafnium, and phosphate sources at a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%; calcining the mixture at 700 degrees C to 900 degrees C; and sintering the calcined powder and forming the oxidation-resistant surface region by an oxygen anneal.
14. The method of claim 13, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.
15. The method of claim 14, wherein the inert gas atmosphere is argon or nitrogen.

16. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer comprises the oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1.
17. The solid-state battery of claim 16, wherein the positive electrode layer further comprises a conductive carbon in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt%.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers and a porosity of 16% or less is provided. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sheet formability. The roll temperature is 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 20 micrometers after calendering. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved sheet formability.

A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%.
2. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1.4 mS/cm or more.
3. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 2, wherein the material is in the form of a powder, a pellet, or a sheet.
4. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C.
5. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, wherein the material has an activation energy for lithium ion conduction of 0.40 eV or less.
6. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.3 MPa or more.
7. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, wherein the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm.
8. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 7, wherein an electronic conductivity of the material at 25 degrees C is 1 x 10^-8 S/cm or less.
9. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 17 micrometers to 27 micrometers.
10. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 14 micrometers to 30 micrometers.
11. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers.
12. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 11, wherein a particle size distribution of the material has a D90 of 20 micrometers or less.
13. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 1.72 wt% to 2.68 wt%.
14. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, wherein a lithium ion transference number of the material is 0.99 or more.
15. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 16% or less.
16. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 15, wherein the material is in the form of particles having a BET specific surface area of 1 m2/g to 20 m2/g.
17. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 50 degrees C to 70 degrees C.

18. A method for producing the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, the method comprising: kneading the solid electrolyte powder with 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% of the binder under shear to fibrillize the binder; rolling the kneaded mixture between rollers at 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C to form a film; and calendering the film to a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers.
19. The method of claim 18, wherein the mixing is performed in a planetary mixer for 10 minutes to 120 minutes.
20. The method of claim 18, further comprising pulverizing the product to a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers.
21. The method of claim 18, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.
22. The method of claim 18, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.

23. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer comprises the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1.
24. The solid-state battery of claim 23, wherein the battery is pressed at a pressure of 1 MPa to 20 MPa during operation.
25. The solid-state battery of claim 23, wherein the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal.
26. The solid-state battery of claim 23, wherein the battery is a laminate cell comprising at least two unit cells stacked in series.
27. The solid-state battery of claim 23, further comprising an intermediate layer disposed between the negative electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobium tantalum oxide formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The Li3InCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobium tantalum oxide formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The Li3InCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on titanium-free NASICON-type oxide and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 83% or more. The oxide particles have a core of the titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in germanium. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li2ZrO3, LLZO, and LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide ceramic ion conductor in which indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. Heat treatment at 250 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 0.84 mS/cm or more. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The halide is applied to the positive electrode active material by a wet coating with an alkoxide-free solution, giving a coated cathode. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 6 mS/cm. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.075 or less. The mixed halogen substitution improves the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window of the solid-state battery.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and production method thereof
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12 and Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries. The sintered body has a relative density of 97%, an average grain size of 10 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The lithium secondary battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved sinterability.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 10 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The tin substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance and simpler handling.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An ionic conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.2 to 1.6. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed bromine-iodine substitution
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y) and to a solid-state battery comprising the same. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 9.6 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. Compared with Li6PS5Br, the iodine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3InCl6 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3InCl6 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium indium chloride, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 40% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.

title: Hafnium-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ion-conductive solid stable above 4.8 V and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. Part of the titanium in the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase is substituted by hafnium in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.8 V. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the sinterability of the electrolyte layer.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and a porosity of 10% or less is provided. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers, a porosity of 5%, a tensile strength of 3 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The method shortens the process and improves the sheet formability and interfacial resistance of the layer.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and a porosity of 10% or less is provided. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers, a porosity of 5%, a tensile strength of 3 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The method shortens the process and improves the sheet formability and interfacial resistance of the layer.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. The LGPS material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The content of P2O5 is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.8 mS/cm or more. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the solid-state lithium battery. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 2.5 mS/cm. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the moisture stability is retained.

title: Hafnium-substituted phosphate-based NASICON ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.8 V and lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor stable against oxidation above 4.8 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LATP material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.8 V. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The oxide ceramic ion conductor enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by arsenic-free antimony substitution is provided. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 5 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). title: Gallium-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and lithium battery
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ceramic ion conductor doped with gallium and sintered with Li3BO3 is described. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1200 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm and a relative density of 96%. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The densification improves the mechanical strength and the grain boundary resistance of the garnet layer.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a solid electrolyte with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.8 MPa or more. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The method shortens the process and improves the cycle life and interfacial resistance of the layer.

2. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C.
3. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, wherein the binder is at least one selected from the group consisting of PTFE, a PTFE copolymer, and ultra-high molecular weight polyethylene.
4. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 5% or less.
5. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 4, further comprising a binder in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt%.
6. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1.8 mS/cm or more.

7. A method for producing the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, the method comprising: kneading the solid electrolyte powder with 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% of the binder under shear to fibrillize the binder; rolling the kneaded mixture between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C to form a film; and calendering the film to a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers.
8. The method of claim 7, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.

9. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer comprises the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1.
10. The solid-state lithium battery of claim 9, wherein the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid that remains stable up to 4.8 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the zirconium substitution and the surface region. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 85%. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The zirconium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the ionic conductivity in contact with lithium.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. In the monoclinic structure, yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The oxidation stability limit is 4.1 V or more and the conductivity is 1.05 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved ionic conductivity and rate capability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tungstate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The Li2ZrO3 and Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The high coverage of the coating results in improved interfacial resistance at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The Li3InCl6, LiNbO3, and Li2ZrO3 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The lithium niobium tantalum oxide shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. When fired at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Compared with Li6PS5Br, the iodine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better moisture stability.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride ion-conductive solid with trigonal structure
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. Heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The material comprises Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the electrochemical window at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body having an average grain size of 2 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. In a solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. When v is 0.5, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction for lithium battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and Li3InCl6. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The coating layer has an average thickness of 10 nm and a coverage of 80%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 30% relative to uncoated particles. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and interfacial resistance and rate capability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The disclosure is applicable to lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3InCl6. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance and rate capability.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the solid electrolyte. The LLZO, LATP, and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. A Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% or more and a critical current density of 1.5 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The silver additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved high-voltage stability and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and lithium battery
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.15 or less. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 500 degrees C. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.1, and the room-temperature conductivity is 9.6 mS/cm. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the lithium secondary battery without a drying step. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and moisture stability.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a lithium fluoride-containing additive layer
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which lithium fluoride is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% to suppress dendrites. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the electronic conductivity of the solid electrolyte layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. A Coulombic efficiency of 98.8% or more and a critical current density of 4 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved cycle life.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a solid electrolyte of high conductivity. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The Li3PS4, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the ionic conductivity is retained.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of scandium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Provided is an orthorhombic halide ceramic ion conductor in which scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ScCl3, and ZrCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.2 to 0.45 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.2 to 0.45. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiF, Li3YCl6, and LiNbO3 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved electrochemical window.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 2 hours. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from tetrahydrofuran, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The reaction at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a solid electrolyte with improved moisture stability.
claims: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more.
2. The method of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 3 micrometers to 10 micrometers.
3. The method of claim 1, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.1 wt% or less.
4. The method of claim 1, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.5 mS/cm or more.
5. The method of claim 4, wherein a carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.5 wt% or less.
6. The method of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 1.5 micrometers to 15 micrometers.
7. The method of claim 1, wherein the reaction temperature is 55 degrees C to 70 degrees C.
8. The method of claim 1, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 430 degrees C to 480 degrees C.
9. The method of claim 1, wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C.
10. The method of claim 1, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less.
11. The method of claim 10, wherein the reacting is performed for 6 hours to 72 hours.
12. A solid electrolyte produced by the method of claim 1.
13. The solid electrolyte of claim 12, wherein the material is in the form of particles having a BET specific surface area of 1 m2/g to 20 m2/g.
14. The solid electrolyte of claim 12, wherein a lithium ion transference number of the material is 0.99 or more.
15. The solid electrolyte of claim 12, wherein the material is in the form of a powder, a pellet, or a sheet.

16. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer comprises the solid electrolyte of claim 12.
17. The all-solid-state lithium battery of claim 16, wherein the positive electrode layer comprises a lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide.
18. The all-solid-state lithium battery of claim 16, further comprising a buffer layer disposed between the negative electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer.
19. The all-solid-state lithium battery of claim 18, wherein the battery is a laminate cell comprising at least two unit cells stacked in series.

title: Germanium-substituted NASICON-type LATP ceramic ion conductor stable above 5.2 V and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor stable against oxidation above 5.2 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more and a conductivity of 0.35 mS/cm or more. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved sinterability.

title: Aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a solid electrolyte layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. The Li3YCl6, LLZO, and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. The Li3YCl6, LLZO, and LiF composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF). The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 300 cycles of stable plating and stripping. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the solid electrolyte at the negative electrode is suppressed and the interfacial resistance is improved.
claims: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.1 micrometers to 10 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 5 nm to 300 nm, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.5% or more.
2. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1.04 micrometers to 1.76 micrometers.
3. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 35 nm to 75 nm.
4. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein an electronic conductivity of the material at 25 degrees C is 1 x 10^-8 S/cm or less.
5. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 99.5% or more.

6. A method for producing the protective layer of claim 1, the method comprising: forming the inorganic layer on the lithium metal by thermal evaporation to a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm; applying a solution containing a fluorine-containing polymer and a lithium salt onto the inorganic layer; and drying the applied solution to form the polymer layer.
7. The method of claim 6, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.
8. The method of claim 6, further comprising pulverizing the product to a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life.
claims: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 35% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium borate and to a method for producing the same. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Suitable compositions include lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and high-voltage stability and rate capability.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2ZrO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2ZrO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. Suitable compositions include lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LiNbO3 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The coating layer has an average thickness of 3 nm and a coverage of 90%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved electrochemical window.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li7P3S11 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The content of SiS2 is 2 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.8 mS/cm or more. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved ionic conductivity and rate performance.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a solid electrolyte film without any solvent. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The binder content is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 0.5 MPa and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film without any solvent. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. A sheet of 80 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery using the sheet shows improved cycle life and a thinner electrolyte layer.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet comprises ceramic ion conductor particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. No solvent is used in the process, so the ceramic ion conductor does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the sheet formability and ionic conductivity.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3BO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6 material. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for preparing the same
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte stable against oxidation above 4.8 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium. Part of the titanium in the perovskite-type LLTO phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.8 V. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The positive electrode active material is LiCoPO4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved interfacial resistance at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte and to a lithium battery including the same. The grain size is 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and the relative density is 91% or more after sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with tungsten and sintered with Li3BO3 is described. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1250 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm and a relative density of 97%. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the grain boundary resistance of the garnet layer.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a solid electrolyte of high conductivity. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li7P3S11, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The Li6PS5Cl and LGPS composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
