title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a niobium-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 94% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The total ionic conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. Examples of the ion conductor include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The method gives reproducible densification and improved sinterability and high-voltage stability at a lower cost.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobium tantalum oxide and to a method for producing the same. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 40% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. The silicon substitution amount is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The silicon content of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 40 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 2.2 mS/cm or more. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of indium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. After dehydration under vacuum at 300 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. A precursor of the Li3InCl6, LiF, and Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the moisture stability.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of indium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. After dehydration under vacuum at 300 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. A precursor of the Li3InCl6, LiF, and Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the moisture stability.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the cycle life.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 500 nm. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the solid-state battery. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The protective layer thickness is 200 nm to 1000 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.5% or more. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by oxygen substitution is provided. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity retention is 90%. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The resulting Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a thio-LISICON phase and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a lithium secondary battery using it. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor and to a lithium battery including the same. A precursor of the LLTO and LATP material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The disclosure is applicable to Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The grain size is 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and the relative density is 94% or more after sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved sinterability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a solid electrolyte film without any solvent. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 100 degrees C to form a continuous film. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4. With a binder content of 3 wt% and a roll temperature of 100 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 16% or less. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved cycle life.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a thio-LISICON phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing GeS2. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.8 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a thio-LISICON phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing GeS2. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.8 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from ethyl propionate, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt%. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in ethyl acetate at 80 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 1 wt%. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the sinterability of the product.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using 1,2-dimethoxyethane and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The LLZO and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li7P3S11. The reaction at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a ceramic ion conductor with improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 5 mol%. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. When v is 0.25, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A sintering aid comprising LiF is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the high-voltage stability of the garnet layer.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: An argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the ionic conductivity of the material is retained after storage.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid electrolyte whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.8 V. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved sinterability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: Provided is a phosphate-based NASICON ceramic ion conductor in which tin substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 83% or more. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The widened electrochemical window improves the sinterability of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer that has a solid content of 50 wt% to 70 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s. The binder is styrene-butadiene rubber in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent heptane. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The binder content is 5 wt%, the drying temperature is 100 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved moisture stability.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 50%. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 4 mS/cm. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the moisture stability of the cell.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and method for producing the same
abstract: An argyrodite solid electrolyte represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3YCl6 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based solid-state battery is described. The coating layer has an average thickness of 3 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance.

title: Negative electrode structure with a lithium fluoride and magnesium nucleation additive layer for suppressing dendrites in a solid-state lithium cell
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a solid-state lithium cell comprises a lithium metal layer, an ion-conductive solid layer comprising Li3PS4 or a garnet-type LLZO, and a nucleation additive layer disposed between them, the additive layer comprising lithium fluoride particles having an average size of 50 nm to 300 nm and magnesium particles in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 90:10 and having a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. During plating, lithium alloys with the magnesium to form uniformly distributed nucleation sites, while the lithium fluoride, which has an electronic conductivity below 1 x 10^-10 S/cm, blocks electron leakage into the ion-conductive solid and prevents the growth of lithium filaments along grain boundaries. During stripping, the alloy phase keeps the contact so that void formation at the interface is suppressed under a stack pressure of 2 MPa to 8 MPa. The structure raises the critical current density at 25 degrees C from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 2.5 mA/cm2 or more, lowers the interfacial resistance to 10 ohm cm2 or less, and keeps the ionic conductivity of the interface. A symmetric cell with the structure survives 500 plating and stripping cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 without short circuit with a Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% or more.

11. The method of claim 10, wherein the pressing is performed at 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with tantalum and sintered with Li2CO3 is described. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. Sintering is performed at 1100 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1100 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm and a relative density of 97%. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiPON layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ceramic ion conductor. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 500 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% over 100 cycles. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The LiPON layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ceramic ion conductor. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved dendrite suppression and interfacial resistance.
claims: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.8% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 200 nm to 1000 nm.
2. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the inorganic layer has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C.
3. The protective layer of claim 2, further comprising a binder in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt%.
4. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the material is substantially free of a liquid component.
5. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 430 nm to 670 nm.
6. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 350 nm to 750 nm.
7. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide.
8. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the material has an activation energy for lithium ion conduction of 0.40 eV or less.
9. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more.

10. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the negative electrode layer comprises the protective layer of claim 1.
11. The lithium secondary battery of claim 10, wherein the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal.
12. The lithium secondary battery of claim 10, wherein the positive electrode layer comprises a lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide.
13. The lithium secondary battery of claim 10, wherein the positive electrode layer further comprises a conductive carbon in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt%.
14. The lithium secondary battery of claim 10, wherein the battery is pressed at a pressure of 1 MPa to 20 MPa during operation.
15. The lithium secondary battery of claim 10, wherein the ceramic ion conductor layer has a thickness of 10 micrometers to 100 micrometers.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state lithium battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 5.2 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 87% or more. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved grain boundary resistance at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

9. The method of claim 8, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.

11. The method of claim 8, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based lithium secondary battery is described. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 50% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance.
claims: 1. 2. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles.
3. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide is suppressed.
4. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 10.5 nm to 22.5 nm.

A method for producing the positive electrode active material of claim 1, the method comprising: preparing a coating solution containing a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobium tantalum oxide; applying the coating solution to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed; and heat-treating the coated core particles at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere.
6. The method of claim 5, further comprising pulverizing the product to a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers.

7. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the positive electrode layer comprises the positive electrode active material of claim 1.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Br6 for lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives an orthorhombic phase with a conductivity of 0.56 mS/cm or more. In a solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and Li3InCl6. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.
claims: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more.
2. The halide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 1.2 micrometers to 4 micrometers.
3. The halide ion-conductive solid of claim 2, wherein a particle size distribution of the material has a D90 of 20 micrometers or less.
4. The halide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein a lithium ion transference number of the material is 0.99 or more.
5. The halide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein a content of carbon in the material is 0.5 wt% or less.
6. The halide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more.

7. A method for producing the halide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing LiBr, InBr3, and HfBr4 in a molar ratio corresponding to the composition; mechanochemically reacting the mixture in a sealed container; and heat-treating the reacted powder at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C under an inert atmosphere.
8. The method of claim 7, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.

9. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer comprises the halide ion-conductive solid of claim 1.
10. The solid-state lithium battery of claim 9, wherein the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an arsenic-free antimony-rich surface region is described. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm and a retention of 70% after humid exposure. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.12 or less. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and electrochemical window.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the grain boundary resistance of the product.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. A solid-state lithium battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ceramic ion conductor. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. A stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 1 mA/cm2. The suppression of void formation improves the ionic conductivity and cycle life during fast charging.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises an orthorhombic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6. The halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.2 V versus Li/Li+. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The zirconium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the moisture stability.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiTaO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based solid-state battery is described. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and interfacial resistance.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the germanium substitution and the surface region. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLZO and LLTO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.8 V. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The oxide solid electrolyte enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in ethyl acetate to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved moisture stability.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. Heat treatment at 200 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives an orthorhombic phase with a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better moisture stability.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Li3N layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by thermal evaporation. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The inorganic layer is formed by thermal evaporation to a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO and LiF material. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Lithium yttrium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3YCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the lithium secondary battery without a drying step. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5Cl material. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 15 nm. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium yttrium chloride, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by oxygen substitution is provided. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The ion-conductive solid shows an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 10 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. A precursor of the Li2ZrO3 and Li3InCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The high coverage of the coating results in improved interfacial resistance at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. A residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. The lithium secondary battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The Li7P3S11 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using acetonitrile
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in acetonitrile at 25 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The solvent is acetonitrile, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved ionic conductivity and sinterability.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12 and Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The total ionic conductivity is 0.42 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The material comprises Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved cycle life compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 4 cm3/g or less. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 2 cm3/g. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The arsenic-free antimony content of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 4 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1.6 mS/cm or more. A solid-state lithium battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder for lithium battery
abstract: A Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which magnesium is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% to suppress dendrites. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 4 mA/cm2. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. In an embodiment the material is Li3YCl6. A stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The method prevents short circuit and improves the ionic conductivity without a thick protective layer.

title: Slurry composition for a ceramic ion conductor layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-butadiene rubber
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer. The binder is styrene-butadiene rubber in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 30 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The slurry has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The LLZO and LATP material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the layer shows improved ionic conductivity and a thin electrolyte layer.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 2.3 mS/cm. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the sinterability are improved.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12 and Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1150 degrees C, and the resulting density is 92%. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. In a solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The Li2ZrO3, LATP, and LLZO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved ionic conductivity and sinterability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiCoPO4. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 83% or more. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. The Li6PS5Cl and LGPS material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The Li6PS5Cl and LGPS composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the moisture stability of the electrolyte layer.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The coating layer has an average thickness of 5 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. Firing is performed at 480 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the cycle life.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium chloride ion-conductive solid prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The oxidation stability limit is 4 V or more and the conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved high-voltage stability and rate capability.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.02 to 0.25, and a method for producing the same are provided. Heat treatment at 200 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives an orthorhombic phase with a conductivity of 1.05 mS/cm or more. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6, LiF, and LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The halide ion-conductive solid is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a NASICON-type LATP ion-conductive solid in which germanium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The Li2ZrO3, LLZO, and LATP material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. Part of the titanium in the NASICON-type LATP phase is substituted by germanium in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. With germanium substitution of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a NASICON-type LATP ion-conductive solid in which germanium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The Li2ZrO3, LLZO, and LATP material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. Part of the titanium in the NASICON-type LATP phase is substituted by germanium in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. With germanium substitution of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
