title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a zinc-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 0.7 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The Li3YCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99% after 100 cycles. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3YCl6. The material comprises Li3YCl6, and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The method prevents short circuit and improves the cycle life without a thick protective layer.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Ag-C layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a solid electrolyte layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 300 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 1 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99% over 100 cycles. The LLZO, LiF, and Li3YCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The inorganic layer is formed by solution casting to a thickness of 120 nm to 600 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved cycle life.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 4.5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. With zirconium substitution of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The LLTO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The oxide particles have a core of the perovskite-type LLTO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in zirconium. The low electronic conductivity of the LLTO material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiPON layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 40 nm to 200 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The LiPON layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The LiPON layer of 100 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6 material. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved cycle life.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a NASICON-type LATP ceramic ion conductor in which zirconium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. The LLTO and LLZO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The oxidation potential is 5.2 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLTO and LLZO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Lithium niobium tantalum oxide-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and Li3InCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coating layer has an average thickness of 8 nm and a coverage of 80%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 30% relative to uncoated particles. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the all-solid-state battery. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 2 hours. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. An H2S generation of 40 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 75% or more are obtained. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11. The ion-conductive solid retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved grain boundary resistance and sinterability.

title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ion-conductive solid particles are dispersed in xylene with a rubber binder and a dispersant. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 15 micrometers. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ion-conductive solid does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. Suitable compositions include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the cycle life of the layer.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by sputtering for lithium battery
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by sputtering followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. The protective layer thickness is 80 nm to 400 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.5% or more. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the solid electrolyte at the negative electrode is suppressed and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2ZrO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. The coating layer has an average thickness of 3 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 60% relative to uncoated particles. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Tin-substituted titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ion-conductive solid stable above 4.5 V
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. Part of the titanium in the titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase is substituted by tin in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more and a conductivity of 0.49 mS/cm or more. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP and LLTO material. The tin substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the high-voltage stability and sinterability in contact with lithium.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNbO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The coating layer has an average thickness of 5 nm and a coverage of 80%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 30% relative to uncoated particles. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet solid electrolyte doped with aluminum and sintered with Li2CO3 is described. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The disclosure is applicable to lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1150 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm and a relative density of 94%. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by solution casting followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 200 nm. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% and no dendrite penetration is observed. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the ceramic ion conductor at the negative electrode is suppressed and the dendrite suppression is improved.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state battery. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The mixed halogen substitution improves the grain boundary resistance and sinterability of the all-solid-state battery.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium scandium chloride ceramic ion conductor with orthorhombic structure for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium scandium chloride ceramic ion conductor prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The material comprises Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.3 V. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the electrochemical window at 4.3 V is improved.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. The ion-conductive component may be Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LGPS and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The SiS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the cycle life and ionic conductivity.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting solid electrolyte film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. The disclosure is applicable to Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The LLTO and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The LLTO and LLZO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The tensile strength is 1.8 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The method shortens the process and improves the sinterability of the layer.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6 and method for preparing the same
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl, LGPS, and Li7P3S11 material. Heat treatment at 250 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved cycle life and rate capability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobium tantalum oxide formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 40% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3InCl6. A solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance and rate capability.

9. The solid-state battery of claim 7, further comprising a buffer layer disposed between the negative electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer.
10. The solid-state battery of claim 7, wherein the battery is a laminate cell comprising at least two unit cells stacked in series.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2ZrO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The coating layer has an average thickness of 15 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.

The coating layer has an average thickness of 15 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride ion-conductive solid with orthorhombic structure and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is an orthorhombic halide ion-conductive solid in which yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives an orthorhombic phase with a conductivity of 1.05 mS/cm or more. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3InCl6. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The halide is applied to the positive electrode active material by a wet coating with an alkoxide-free solution, giving a coated cathode. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the electrochemical window.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium metal layer, a ceramic ion conductor layer, and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The Li3YCl6 and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. With the additive in an amount of 1 wt% and a stack pressure of 10 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5%. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. In an embodiment the material is Li3YCl6 and beta-Li3PS4. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3YCl6 and Li3PS4 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. A stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved interfacial resistance and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on titanium-free NASICON-type oxide and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.3 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5 V. The LLZO and LLTO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The oxide particles have a core of the titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The oxide solid electrolyte enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and moisture stability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium yttrium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium yttrium chloride and to a method for producing the same. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 50 mol% or more. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6 and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a NASICON-type LATP ion-conductive solid in which hafnium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A capacity retention of 80% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The oxide particles have a core of the NASICON-type LATP phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The oxide particles have a core of the phosphate-based NASICON phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in germanium. Part of the titanium in the phosphate-based NASICON phase is substituted by germanium in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLTO and Li2ZrO3 material. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. With germanium substitution of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved grain boundary resistance at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. After exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity retention is 70%. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 material. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The ceramic ion conductor retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5% after 100 cycles. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The additive comprises indium in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Li3N layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a Li3N inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99% and no dendrite penetration is observed. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The inorganic layer is formed by thermal evaporation to a thickness of 40 nm to 200 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved dendrite suppression and cycle life.

title: Ceramic ion conductor slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The binder content of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% gives a peel strength of 0.1 N/cm or more and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The LiF and Li3YCl6 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. A precursor of the LiF and Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved cycle life.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for producing the same
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by oxygen substitution is provided. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted Li6PS5X having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li3YCl6, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 20 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LiF, LLZO, and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the lithium secondary battery. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li3YCl6. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the interfacial resistance.

The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 20 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LiF, LLZO, and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the lithium secondary battery. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li3YCl6. title: Self-supporting solid electrolyte sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a solid electrolyte sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state battery without a drying step. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LATP, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The roll temperature is 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 20 micrometers after calendering. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. An all-solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved sheet formability and a thinner electrolyte layer.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa with a zinc additive. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6, Li3PS4, and LLZO material. A halide coating is compatible with the solid electrolyte because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99% after 100 cycles. A stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-P2O5 glass. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 30% to 65% by X-ray diffraction. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the lithium secondary battery. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of scandium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which titanium is substituted for part of the scandium in a lithium scandium chloride framework. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF). Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the solid-state battery. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF material. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.3 micrometers to 3 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The median particle diameter D50 is 1 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 3 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a solid electrolyte sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and beta-Li3PS4, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. With a binder content of 3 wt% and a roll temperature of 120 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 20% or less. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the LATP and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A solid-state lithium battery using the sheet shows improved ionic conductivity and a thinner electrolyte layer.

title: Lithium indium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm is provided. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 5 nm. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The lithium indium chloride shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the interfacial resistance.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium erbium chloride solid electrolyte with orthorhombic structure and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Described is a lithium erbium chloride solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. In the orthorhombic structure, erbium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved ionic conductivity and rate capability.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A garnet solid electrolyte sintered body having an average grain size of 5 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The total ionic conductivity is 0.42 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. title: Wet coating method for forming a solid electrolyte layer on a release film and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 15 micrometers. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The binder is polyisobutylene in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent xylene. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the cycle life of the cell.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ion-conductive solid film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. The lithium secondary battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The Li3PS4, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. A sheet of 80 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Li3N layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a ceramic ion conductor layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The inorganic layer is formed by sputtering to a thickness of 40 nm to 200 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The protective layer thickness is 40 nm to 200 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.5% or more. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The LiF, Li3YCl6, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance of the lithium metal battery.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 550 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved sinterability and ionic conductivity.

11. The moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 10, wherein the material has a true density of 1.8 g/cm3 to 5.5 g/cm3.
12. The moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 70% or more.

13. 14. The method of claim 13, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.
15. The method of claim 13, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.
16. The method of claim 13, wherein the method is performed in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.

18. The method of claim 13, wherein the inert gas atmosphere is argon or nitrogen.
19. The method of claim 18, wherein the mixing is performed in a planetary mixer for 10 minutes to 120 minutes.
20. The method of claim 13, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.

title: Aluminum-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 5 mol%. A solid-state battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1150 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm and a relative density of 92%. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved high-voltage stability.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by atomic layer deposition and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a LiPON inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99% and no dendrite penetration is observed. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The LiPON layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the interfacial resistance of the lithium metal battery.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The LiNbO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window and interfacial resistance.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 10 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The high coverage of the coating results in improved grain boundary resistance at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Described is a lithium erbium chloride ion-conductive solid prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The Li3YCl6, LiF, and Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ErCl3, and TiCl4 followed by heat treatment at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3InCl6. The oxidation stability limit is 4.3 V or more and the conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved electrochemical window and moisture stability.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid electrolyte whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The oxide particles have a core of the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in zirconium. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the lithium secondary battery. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 85% or more. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved sinterability.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a silver-containing additive layer
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which a silver-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The critical current density is 1 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 100 cycles or more. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved electrochemical window.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using an indium-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium metal layer, an ion-conductive solid layer, and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 1.5 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 500 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. The additive comprises indium in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved ionic conductivity and cycle life.

title: Slurry composition for a ceramic ion conductor layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ceramic ion conductor particles are dispersed in a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane with a rubber binder and a dispersant. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The powder used for the sheet is prepared by a wet-chemical synthesis with filtration and drying, and the moisture exposure is controlled by a dew point of -40 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LLZO and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ceramic ion conductor does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The slurry has a solid content of 70 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 30 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and production method thereof
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours, the conductivity retention is 90%. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity and simpler handling.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and production method thereof
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours, the conductivity retention is 90%. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity and simpler handling.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. The arsenic-free antimony content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 20 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1 mS/cm or more. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the sinterability.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. With hafnium substitution of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The Li2ZrO3 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved sinterability.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid oxygen binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 2.3 mS/cm. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the sinterability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 5 nm. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. Specific examples are Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the electrochemical window is improved.
