title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 80:20 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS and Li3PS4 material. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 70%. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. The Li2O addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. The Li7P3S11 and LGPS composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. A solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the cycle life of the cell.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet comprises ceramic ion conductor particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ceramic ion conductor layer onto an electrode of the lithium secondary battery without a drying step. The binder content is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 1 MPa and a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.12 or less. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to a solid-state lithium battery comprising the same. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.12 or less. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better moisture stability.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: An argyrodite solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. When fired at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.12 or less. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity and cycle life.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. The LLZO, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The solvent is acetonitrile, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. A residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the moisture stability and sinterability.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant aluminum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The total ionic conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.05 to 0.4, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the moisture stability.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant aluminum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The total ionic conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.05 to 0.4, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the moisture stability.

title: Hafnium-substituted titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.8 V and production method thereof
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor stable against oxidation above 4.8 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.3 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.8 V. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Part of the titanium in the titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase is substituted by hafnium in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the sinterability is improved.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The material comprises Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. Specific examples are Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours, the conductivity retention is 70%. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the high-voltage stability.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of scandium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ceramic ion conductor with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. Specific examples are Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6. Heat treatment at 200 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 1.05 mS/cm or more. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. In a solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ceramic ion conductor. The lithium fluoride additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The cell shows no short circuit for 1000 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 2 MPa. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the sinterability.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using tetrahydrofuran and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 4.1 mS/cm. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Germanium-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ceramic ion conductor stable above 5.2 V and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5.2 V. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a tin-rich surface region is described. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. Specific examples are argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 60% or more are obtained. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the sinterability and ionic conductivity.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Br6, wherein z is 0.3 to 0.55, and a method for producing the same are provided. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 3 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. Specific examples are Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved high-voltage stability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm is provided. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. Suitable compositions include lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved high-voltage stability.

9. The positive electrode active material of claim 8, wherein the material has a water content of 0.5 wt% or less as measured by Karl Fischer titration.

A method for producing the positive electrode active material of claim 1, the method comprising: preparing a coating solution containing a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate; applying the coating solution to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed; and heat-treating the coated core particles at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere.
11. The method of claim 10, further comprising pulverizing the product to a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ion-conductive solid shows improved cycle life and ionic conductivity compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Aluminum-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Sintering at 1230 degrees C with a lithium excess of 8 mol% gives a relative density of 92% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.05 to 0.4, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to a solid-state battery comprising the same. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The Li6PS5Cl and LGPS material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. A solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 4.2 mS/cm. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and electrochemical window.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and production method thereof
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the germanium substitution and the surface region. The oxidation potential is 5.2 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved sinterability and high-voltage stability.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ceramic ion conductor containing a thio-LISICON phase and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state lithium battery. The content of P2O5 is 2 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.8 mS/cm or more. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state lithium battery. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the cycle life and ionic conductivity.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer that has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The LLZO material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The binder content is 2 wt%, the drying temperature is 100 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ceramic ion conductor does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the ionic conductivity and sheet formability of the layer.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer that has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The LLZO material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The binder content is 2 wt%, the drying temperature is 100 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ceramic ion conductor does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the ionic conductivity and sheet formability of the layer.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and method for producing the same
abstract: A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12 and Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1230 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm and a relative density of 97%. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the high-voltage stability of the garnet layer.

title: Gallium-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. Sintering at 1150 degrees C with a lithium excess of 15 mol% gives a relative density of 92% and a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li7P3S11 phase and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li7P3S11 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 60%. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 40% to 75% by X-ray diffraction. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the cycle life is improved.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. The particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and the layer has a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The binder is hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent anisole. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the cycle life and interfacial resistance of the layer.

title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ion-conductive solid does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The particles have a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and the layer has a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Zirconium-substituted NASICON-type LATP solid electrolyte stable above 5 V and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The widened electrochemical window improves the grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a beta-Li3PS4 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. The Li3PS4 and LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3PS4 and LGPS material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.

title: Tin-substituted titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.5 V and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on titanium-free NASICON-type oxide and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the solid-state battery. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. With tin substitution of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. Part of the titanium in the titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase is substituted by tin in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 and LLZO material. The oxide ceramic ion conductor enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the sinterability and ionic conductivity.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa with an indium additive. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 1.5 mA/cm2. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and lithium fluoride (LiF). A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4 and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The method prevents short circuit and improves the cycle life without a thick protective layer.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 80%. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 75% or more. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO and LATP material. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved sinterability.

title: Germanium-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.5 V and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The germanium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the ionic conductivity in contact with lithium.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. The oxygen content of 1 mol% to 4 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 40 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1 mS/cm or more. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the ionic conductivity.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a thio-LISICON phase and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 72:28 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state battery. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide solid electrolyte whose decomposition current at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. With tin substitution of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The oxide particles have a core of the phosphate-based NASICON phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in tin. The widened electrochemical window improves the grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide solid electrolyte whose decomposition current at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. With tin substitution of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The oxide particles have a core of the phosphate-based NASICON phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in tin. The widened electrochemical window improves the grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved moisture stability.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide solid electrolyte that does not require long mechanical milling. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The reaction at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solvent is tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the sinterability of the product.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3InCl6 shell with high coverage and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved electrochemical window.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. Specific examples are Li7P3S11. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The SiS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the electrochemical window.

title: Ion-conductive solid sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet having a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and a porosity of 20% or less is provided. The binder content is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 1 MPa and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material. No solvent is used in the process, so the ion-conductive solid does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The method shortens the process and improves the sheet formability of the layer.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ceramic ion conductor comprises a monoclinic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 material. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.3 micrometers to 3 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.2 V versus Li/Li+. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The halide ceramic ion conductor is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the moisture stability.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ion-conductive solid in which hafnium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium bromide framework. The material comprises Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved ionic conductivity and rate capability.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 60% or more are obtained. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the lithium secondary battery. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved grain boundary resistance and sinterability.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A capacity retention of 88% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a tin-rich surface region is described. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. A precursor of the LLZO, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 20 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The tin substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the sinterability.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 7.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 500 degrees C. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.12 or less. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The mixed halogen substitution improves the moisture stability of the solid-state lithium battery.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The disclosure is applicable to Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The widened electrochemical window improves the sinterability and ionic conductivity of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 3.1 mS/cm. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A solid electrolyte sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and a lithium secondary battery including the sheet are described. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The LLZO and LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The tensile strength is 0.6 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the interfacial resistance of the cell.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobium tantalum oxide, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobium tantalum oxide, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium borate and to a method for producing the same. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The LiNbO3, Li3InCl6, and Li2ZrO3 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted Li6PS5X having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X solid electrolyte and lithium battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.15 or less. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the lithium secondary battery. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a niobium-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 91% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1100 degrees C, and the resulting density is 94%. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. Sintering is performed at 1100 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. Examples of the ion conductor include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The method gives reproducible densification and improved grain boundary resistance at a lower cost.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 40% to 75% by X-ray diffraction. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The solid electrolyte shows improved ionic conductivity compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiTaO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium fluoride (LiF). A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl, LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and LiF material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 70 mol% or more. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and electrochemical window and rate capability.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and method for producing the same
abstract: An argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.12 or less. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and moisture stability.
