title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2WO4 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The coating layer has an average thickness of 8 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability.

2. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein an electronic conductivity of the material at 25 degrees C is 1 x 10^-8 S/cm or less.
3. The positive electrode active material of claim 2, wherein the material has a true density of 1.8 g/cm3 to 5.5 g/cm3.
4. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 104% or more.
5. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the material has a water content of 0.5 wt% or less as measured by Karl Fischer titration.
6. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C.
7. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.
8. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 6.9 nm to 10.7 nm.
9. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 3 micrometers to 10 micrometers.
10. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the core particles are secondary particles having an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers.
11. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 44% or more.
12. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein a particle size distribution of the material has a D90 of 20 micrometers or less.
13. The positive electrode active material of claim 12, wherein the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less.

14. A method for producing the positive electrode active material of claim 1, the method comprising: preparing a coating solution containing a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate; applying the coating solution to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed; and heat-treating the coated core particles at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere.
15. The method of claim 14, wherein the method is performed in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.
16. The method of claim 14, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.
17. The method of claim 14, wherein the mixing is performed in a planetary mixer for 10 minutes to 120 minutes.

An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the positive electrode layer comprises the positive electrode active material of claim 1.
19. The all-solid-state battery of claim 18, wherein the positive electrode layer further comprises a conductive carbon in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt%.
20. The all-solid-state battery of claim 18, wherein the battery is a laminate cell comprising at least two unit cells stacked in series.
21. The all-solid-state battery of claim 18, wherein the solid electrolyte layer has a thickness of 10 micrometers to 100 micrometers.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.12 or less. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. When fired at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and moisture stability.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3PS4, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sinterability.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 4 cm3/g or less. The arsenic-free antimony content of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 4 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 0.7 mS/cm or more. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the sinterability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ceramic ion conductor film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. The Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The binder content is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 2 MPa and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the cycle life and sheet formability of the cell.

title: Tin-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ceramic ion conductor stable above 5.2 V and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5.2 V. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLZO and LLTO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours, the conductivity retention is 70%. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the grain boundary resistance.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a silver-containing additive layer
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa with a silver additive. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 1 mA/cm2. The silver additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 250 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and LiF material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. After dehydration under vacuum at 250 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, YCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.

abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which an indium-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 4 mA/cm2. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on phosphate-based NASICON and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 80%. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an arsenic-free antimony-rich surface region is described. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity and simpler handling.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 80% or more. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The tin substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance in contact with lithium.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X solid electrolyte having anion disorder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. An ionic conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.2 to 1.6. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 550 degrees C. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life and moisture stability.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 500 degrees C. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.1, and the room-temperature conductivity is 4.2 mS/cm. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. After heat treatment at 320 degrees C for 5 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 3.1 mS/cm. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 500 degrees C. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid in which part of the bromine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4. With tin substitution of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The low electronic conductivity of the Li2ZrO3 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The solid content is 30 wt% to 50 wt%, the viscosity is 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved cycle life.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on NASICON-type LATP and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 83% or more. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. A solid-state battery comprising the Li2ZrO3, LLZO, and LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The oxide particles have a core of the NASICON-type LATP phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in zirconium. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability of the electrolyte layer.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3BO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The average thickness of the coating is 6 nm to 30 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 60%. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. The ion-conductive solid may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4 and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 4 mS/cm. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by oxygen substitution is provided. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The oxygen substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 75% or more are obtained. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the ionic conductivity.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance and electrochemical window.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet having a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and a porosity of 20% or less is provided. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. The LATP and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The LATP and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The material comprises Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. A precursor of the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 75% or more and an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm is provided. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 75% or more and an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm is provided. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The disclosure is applicable to lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life and interfacial resistance.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The all-solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The lithium tungstate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tantalum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1200 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a relative density of 94%. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The method gives reproducible densification and improved sinterability at a lower cost.

title: Niobium-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and method for preparing the same
abstract: A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12 and Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The total ionic conductivity is 0.42 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the sinterability is improved.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Described is a lithium scandium chloride solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The median particle diameter D50 is 3 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 200 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the high-voltage stability at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ion-conductive solid with an oxidation limit of 4.7 V or more is described. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A capacity retention of 90% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3, LLZO, and LLTO material. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability of the electrolyte layer.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2ZrO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2ZrO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. Specific examples are Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and LiF composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The lithium zirconate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The inorganic layer is formed by solution casting to a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99% and no dendrite penetration is observed. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The LiPON layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ion-conductive solid. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing P2O5. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 70%. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved ionic conductivity and rate performance.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an ion-conductive solid whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the LATP and LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the germanium substitution and the surface region. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. A capacity retention of 90% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The germanium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability in contact with lithium.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). In a solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. A capacity retention of 90% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). In a solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. A capacity retention of 90% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet having a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and a porosity of 10% or less is provided. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. With a binder content of 3 wt% and a roll temperature of 80 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 10% or less. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LATP and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the interfacial resistance of the cell.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium metal layer, a ceramic ion conductor layer, and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99.3% after 100 cycles. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the solid-state battery. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The Li3PS4, LLZO, and Li3YCl6 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved cycle life and dendrite suppression.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.12 or less. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. When fired at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.

title: Dendrite-suppressing indium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell for lithium battery
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 1.4 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the dendrite suppression. A Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% or more and a critical current density of 2 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the dendrite suppression is improved.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An H2S generation of 40 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 70% or more are obtained. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An H2S generation of 40 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 70% or more are obtained. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film
abstract: A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer comprises ceramic ion conductor particles, a styrene-butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 80 degrees C to 120 degrees C in an oven. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% and a viscosity of 3000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 30 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. A lithium secondary battery using the layer shows improved ionic conductivity and a thin electrolyte layer.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and production method thereof
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 4.5 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the moisture stability.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 97% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the high-voltage stability of the garnet layer.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The oxidation potential is 5.2 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 5 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The Li2ZrO3 and LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The lithium niobate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 200 cycles of stable plating and stripping. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 50 nm. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The LiPON layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ceramic ion conductor. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the interfacial resistance and cycle life of the lithium metal battery.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. A solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The resulting Li6PS5Cl material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 5 mS/cm. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the electrochemical window of the product.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with tungsten and sintered with Al2O3 is described. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A sintering aid comprising Al2O3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The total ionic conductivity is 0.42 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Germanium-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.5 V and lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.5 V. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state lithium battery. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The LATP and LLTO material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the sinterability is improved.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm is provided. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Tin-substituted titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.8 V and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on titanium-free NASICON-type oxide and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. Specific examples are lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.3 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.8 V. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiNbO3, Li6PS5Cl, and LiF material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the lithium secondary battery. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. The tin substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the interfacial resistance and electrochemical window in contact with lithium.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor and to a lithium battery including the same. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO and Li2ZrO3 material. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.15 to 0.5, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the grain boundary resistance is improved.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in tetrahydrofuran at 40 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The suspension concentration is 15 wt%, the reaction temperature is 40 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 120 degrees C. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the sinterability of the product.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran at 40 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The reaction at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The protective layer thickness is 120 nm to 600 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 97.8% or more. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The bilayer structure improves the moisture stability compared with a single inorganic layer.

3. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 500 cycles or more.
4. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.8% or more.

6. The lithium secondary battery of claim 5, wherein the positive electrode layer comprises a lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. Firing is performed at 480 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the lithium secondary battery without a drying step. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability and electrochemical window.

2. The sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 470 degrees C to 500 degrees C.
3. The sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein 0.1 <= x <= 0.55.
4. The sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the material is in the form of a powder, a pellet, or a sheet.
5. The sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 4, wherein a content of carbon in the material is 0.5 wt% or less.
6. The sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 5, wherein the material is in the form of particles having a BET specific surface area of 1 m2/g to 20 m2/g.

7. A method for producing the sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, LiCl, and LiI at a molar ratio corresponding to the composition to obtain a precursor mixture; mechanically milling the precursor mixture; and firing the milled mixture at 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C in an inert gas atmosphere.
8. The method of claim 7, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.
9. The method of claim 7, wherein the mixing is performed in a planetary mixer for 10 minutes to 120 minutes.
