title: Li6PS5X sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. Firing is performed at 480 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the lithium secondary battery without a drying step. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability and electrochemical window.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.

title: Lithium indium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3InCl6 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium indium chloride, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and to a method of handling it in a dry room. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 3.2 mS/cm. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li7P3S11. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the grain boundary resistance are improved.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer that has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ceramic ion conductor does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 50 micrometers. The binder is hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent heptane. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved cycle life.

3. The slurry of claim 1, wherein the solvent is at least one selected from the group consisting of xylene, heptane, anisole, toluene, and butyl butyrate.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiCoPO4. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 88%. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The Li2ZrO3, LATP, and LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The oxide ion-conductive solid enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiCoPO4. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 88%. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The Li2ZrO3, LATP, and LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The oxide ion-conductive solid enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Niobium-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. Sintering is performed at 1200 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). When v is 0.3, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO, LLTO, and LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 3 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, LiF, and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ScCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the electrochemical window.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3YCl6 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3YCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coating layer has an average thickness of 10 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability and cycle life.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ion-conductive solid in which zirconium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium bromide framework. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 200 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.3 to 0.55. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the electrochemical window at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The LGPS and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.045 or less. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and moisture stability.

title: Tin-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ceramic ion conductor stable above 5 V and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The LATP material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The oxidation potential is 5 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The oxide particles have a core of the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in tin. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the ionic conductivity of the electrolyte layer.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using tetrahydrofuran for lithium battery
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO, Li7P3S11, and LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C after drying at 180 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved moisture stability and sinterability.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and method for preparing the same
abstract: An argyrodite solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 4.2 mS/cm. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The Li7P3S11 and LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.12 or less. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.

title: Slurry composition for a solid electrolyte layer using a nonpolar solvent and hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer that has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The slurry has a solid content of 70 wt% and a viscosity of 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 15 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C in an oven. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the layer shows improved interfacial resistance and a thin electrolyte layer.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: A garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body having an average grain size of 5 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. Suitable compositions include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the sinterability of the garnet layer.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant niobium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The LATP and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The dopant niobium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1100 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a relative density of 94%. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a solid-state lithium battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A precursor of the LGPS and Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability and electrochemical window.

abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte and to a lithium battery including the same. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP, LLTO, and Li2ZrO3 material. The dopant tungsten occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.1 to 0.45, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1100 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm and a relative density of 94%. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the ionic conductivity.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 90% or more and an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm is provided. The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 75:25 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 30% to 65% by X-ray diffraction. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The LiI addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the electrochemical window.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 75% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 1 hours. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 2 cm3/g. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 1 hours. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved grain boundary resistance and moisture stability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an arsenic-free antimony-rich surface region is described. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted Li6PS5X having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The all-solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.6 mS/cm or more. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-P2O5 glass. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution for lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The Li7P3S11 and LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and electrochemical window.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to a lithium secondary battery comprising the same. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The mixed halogen substitution improves the electrochemical window of the lithium secondary battery.

title: Dendrite-suppressing magnesium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell for lithium battery
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. With the additive in an amount of 0.5 wt% and a stack pressure of 10 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5%. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The resulting LLZO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The additive comprises magnesium in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the cycle life of the solid-state cell.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The oxygen substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.1 mS/cm or more. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. The Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the moisture stability.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The method further comprises a synthesis step in which a solvate complex is precipitated and heat-treated to obtain the powder. The particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and the layer has a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The wet film is dried at 100 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state lithium battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ceramic ion conductor does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using an indium-containing additive layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. A Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% or more and a critical current density of 1.5 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the moisture stability is improved.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 40 nm to 200 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 100 nm. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the solid-state battery. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF), beta-Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6. The LiF layer of 100 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), beta-Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved dendrite suppression.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state lithium battery. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The solvent is a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The ion-conductive solid obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 1 wt%. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the moisture stability.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li7P3S11 phase and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li7P3S11 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing SiS2. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 320 degrees C. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The Li3PS4 and LGPS material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The ion-conductive solid shows improved moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. After exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity retention is 90%. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The material comprises Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. The oxygen substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the grain boundary resistance and moisture stability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the iodine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 92% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. When v is 0.25, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LATP material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by sputtering followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99% and no dendrite penetration is observed. The inorganic layer is formed by sputtering to a thickness of 40 nm to 200 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the cycle life of the lithium metal battery.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tungstate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3, LiNbO3, and Li6PS5Cl material. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a Li3N inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The protective layer thickness is 40 nm to 200 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 97.8% or more. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and lithium battery
abstract: An argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.1, and the room-temperature conductivity is 8.5 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a magnesium-containing additive layer
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which magnesium is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% to suppress dendrites. The critical current density is 1.4 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 250 cycles or more. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 and LLZO material. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The additive comprises magnesium in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The method prevents short circuit and improves the dendrite suppression and interfacial resistance without a thick protective layer.

abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which magnesium is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% to suppress dendrites. The critical current density is 1.4 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 250 cycles or more. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 and LLZO material. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The additive comprises magnesium in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The method prevents short circuit and improves the dendrite suppression and interfacial resistance without a thick protective layer.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and lithium battery
abstract: An argyrodite-type solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. An ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.3 to 0.75. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The solid electrolyte provides improved ionic conductivity and cycle life compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.

title: Slurry composition for an ion-conductive solid layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ion-conductive solid particles are dispersed in xylene with a rubber binder and a dispersant. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state lithium battery. The slurry has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO and LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C has a thickness of 30 micrometers. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from ethyl acetate, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved sinterability.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LATP composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 4.5 mS/cm. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The ion-conductive solid may comprise beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 2 hours. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of yttrium and titanium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.5 V. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.1 to 0.35. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, YCl3, and TiCl4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better moisture stability.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of yttrium and titanium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.5 V. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.1 to 0.35. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, YCl3, and TiCl4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better moisture stability.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using 1,2-dimethoxyethane
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a solid electrolyte with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a ceramic ion conductor with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.8 MPa or more. No solvent is used in the process, so the ceramic ion conductor does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved ionic conductivity and sheet formability.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and a lithium secondary battery including the sheet are described. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The roll temperature is 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 30 micrometers after calendering. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The method shortens the process and improves the ionic conductivity and sheet formability of the layer.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ion-conductive solid particles are dispersed in a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane with a rubber binder and a dispersant. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 1.3 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 20 micrometers. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C in an oven. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The wet film is dried at 80 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved sinterability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air for lithium battery
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 3.2 mS/cm. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobium tantalum oxide and to a method for producing the same. The material comprises Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. When v is 0.4, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved high-voltage stability.

title: Method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% and a viscosity of 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 50 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The wet film is dried at 100 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and beta-Li3PS4. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and a porosity of 30% or less is provided. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3PS4 and LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. No solvent is used in the process, so the solid electrolyte does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers, a porosity of 15%, a tensile strength of 2 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from acetonitrile, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the moisture stability.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ion-conductive solid particles are dispersed in heptane with a rubber binder and a dispersant. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The binder content is 5 wt%, the drying temperature is 100 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. The wet film is dried at 100 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Tin-substituted titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ion-conductive solid stable above 5.2 V and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. With tin substitution of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The positive electrode active material is a 5 V spinel, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ion-conductive solid. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4, Li3YCl6, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using ethyl propionate and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The oxygen content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 4 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 2.2 mS/cm or more. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium borate and to a method for producing the same. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The Li6PS5Cl, Li2ZrO3, and LiNbO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
