title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ion-conductive solid comprises a trigonal crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Br6. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. After dehydration under vacuum at 250 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The material comprises Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li7P3S11, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. Suitable compositions include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by thermal evaporation followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 500 cycles of stable plating and stripping. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the ceramic ion conductor at the negative electrode is suppressed and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a Li7P3S11 phase for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li7P3S11 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 80%. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li7P3S11, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ceramic ion conductor. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. A Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% or more and a critical current density of 1 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 material. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the cycle life.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of indium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which zirconium is substituted for part of the indium in a lithium indium chloride framework. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3InCl6. When z is 0.1, the conductivity is 3 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. In the monoclinic structure, indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The material comprises Li3InCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.

A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ceramic ion conductor doped with tungsten and sintered with LiF is described. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLTO and LATP material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. A sintering aid comprising LiF is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The grain size is 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and the relative density is 94% or more after sintering at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the high-voltage stability of the garnet layer.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. After heat treatment at 280 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 5.5 mS/cm. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is thio-LISICON, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the moisture stability of the cell.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. A precursor of the Li3InCl6 and LiNbO3 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance and high-voltage stability.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25 and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated therein. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm is provided. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The LiNbO3 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 50% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite solid electrolyte having anion disorder and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The Li6PS5Cl, LGPS, and Li3PS4 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 500 degrees C. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. Firing is performed at 500 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for preparing the same
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by oxygen substitution is provided. The Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the all-solid-state battery. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C gives a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The ion-conductive solid retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved grain boundary resistance and moisture stability.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of yttrium and zirconium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.3 V. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6 and LiF material. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid arsenic-free antimony binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 4.5 mS/cm. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.

The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 4.5 mS/cm. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.

2. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the substituting element is at least one selected from the group consisting of Sn, Sb, Si, and O.
3. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 0.6 micrometers to 2 micrometers.
4. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours is 85% or more.
5. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the material has an activation energy for lithium ion conduction of 0.40 eV or less.
6. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 530 degrees C to 580 degrees C.
7. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein a content of carbon in the material is 0.5 wt% or less.
8. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the material is in the form of a powder, a pellet, or a sheet.

9. A method for producing the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, and an arsenic-free antimony source at a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%; amorphizing the mixture by mechanical milling in a dry room having a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower; and heat-treating the amorphized mixture at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere.
10. The method of claim 9, wherein the inert gas atmosphere is argon or nitrogen.
11. The method of claim 9, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.
12. The method of claim 9, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.

title: Wet coating method for forming a solid electrolyte layer on a release film and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The binder content is 3 wt%, the drying temperature is 120 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. A halide coating is compatible with the solid electrolyte because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% to 60 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state lithium battery. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved sheet formability.

8. The method of claim 7, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.
9. The method of claim 8, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.
10. The method of claim 7, wherein the mixing is performed in a planetary mixer for 10 minutes to 120 minutes.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 5.5 mS/cm. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window.

6. The sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 0.6 micrometers to 2 micrometers.
7. The sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 252 degrees C to 273 degrees C.
8. The sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the material has a true density of 1.8 g/cm3 to 5.5 g/cm3.

9. A method for producing the sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: melting or mechanically amorphizing a mixture of Li2S, P2S5, and P2O5 to obtain a vitreous precursor; quenching the precursor to obtain a glass; and heat-treating the glass at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours to precipitate the crystal phase.
10. The method of claim 9, wherein the mixing is performed in a planetary mixer for 10 minutes to 120 minutes.
11. The method of claim 10, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.
12. The method of claim 9, wherein the inert gas atmosphere is argon or nitrogen.

14. The method of claim 9, further comprising pulverizing the product to a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers.

title: Self-supporting ceramic ion conductor sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet having a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers and a porosity of 10% or less is provided. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The binder content is 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 1 MPa and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The method further comprises a synthesis step in which a solvate complex is precipitated and heat-treated to obtain the powder. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved sheet formability.

2. The free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet of claim 1, wherein the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm.
3. The free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet of claim 1, wherein the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet has a roll temperature of 110 degrees C to 130 degrees C.
4. The free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet of claim 1, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 14 micrometers to 30 micrometers.
5. The free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet of claim 4, wherein the material has a true density of 1.8 g/cm3 to 5.5 g/cm3.
6. The free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet of claim 1, wherein the material has an activation energy for lithium ion conduction of 0.40 eV or less.
7. The free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet of claim 1, wherein the material is stored in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.

8. A method for producing the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet of claim 1, the method comprising: kneading the ceramic ion conductor powder with 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% of the binder under shear to fibrillize the binder; rolling the kneaded mixture between rollers at 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C to form a film; and calendering the film to a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers.
9. The method of claim 8, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.
10. The method of claim 9, wherein the method is performed in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.
11. The method of claim 8, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type solid electrolyte having anion disorder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. An ionic conductivity of 7.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.2 to 0.65. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and moisture stability.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tungstate and to a method for producing the same. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 50% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 material. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved interfacial resistance and electrochemical window.

A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 35% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.8 nm to 40 nm.
2. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 60% or more.
3. The positive electrode active material of claim 2, wherein the material is in the form of particles having a BET specific surface area of 1 m2/g to 20 m2/g.
4. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the coating layer is amorphous as confirmed by transmission electron microscopy.
5. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers.
6. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the core particles are secondary particles having an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tungstate and to a method for producing the same. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 50% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 material. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved interfacial resistance and electrochemical window.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from ethyl acetate, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The electrode mixture of the solid-state lithium battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using 1,2-dimethoxyethane and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C after drying at 200 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. The Li3PS4, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved grain boundary resistance and sinterability.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Tungsten-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density and production method thereof
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 95% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. Sintering is performed at 1100 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The dopant tungsten occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The total ionic conductivity is 0.42 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Lithium indium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium indium chloride, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The coating layer has an average thickness of 10 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Lithium indium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium indium chloride, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The coating layer has an average thickness of 10 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 15 mol%. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The dopant gallium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.35 to 0.7, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The LLZO and LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1100 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a relative density of 95%. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the sinterability.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Lithium borate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li3BO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The average thickness of the coating is 4 nm to 20 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The suspension concentration is 10 wt%, the reaction temperature is 40 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the lithium secondary battery. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The arsenic-free antimony content of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 20 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1 mS/cm or more. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the moisture stability.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the moisture stability and sinterability.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body having an average grain size of 5 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Sintering is performed at 1150 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. Sintering at 1150 degrees C with a lithium excess of 10 mol% gives a relative density of 96% and a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the grain boundary resistance of the garnet layer.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using ethyl acetate and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from ethyl acetate, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The protective layer thickness is 20 nm to 100 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 97.8% or more. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved cycle life and dendrite suppression.

title: Gallium-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant gallium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The LATP, Li2ZrO3, and LLTO material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The method gives reproducible densification and improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity at a lower cost.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: An argyrodite ion-conductive solid represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.

title: Solid electrolyte slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which solid electrolyte particles are dispersed in butyl butyrate with a rubber binder and a dispersant. The solid content is 50 wt% to 70 wt%, the viscosity is 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the solid electrolyte does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state battery. The Li3YCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the electrochemical window and moisture stability of the layer.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The Li6PS5Cl, LGPS, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 8.5 mS/cm. Specific examples are argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a lithium secondary battery using it. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The content of Li2O is 3 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.8 mS/cm or more. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The Li2O addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 75:25 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The low electronic conductivity of the Li6PS5Cl material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The LiI addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the cycle life.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. Sintering at 1200 degrees C with a lithium excess of 8 mol% gives a relative density of 95% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved sinterability and high-voltage stability.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a perovskite-type LLTO ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more and a conductivity of 0.21 mS/cm or more. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A lithium secondary battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The oxide particles have a core of the perovskite-type LLTO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved sinterability.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a perovskite-type LLTO ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more and a conductivity of 0.21 mS/cm or more. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A lithium secondary battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The oxide particles have a core of the perovskite-type LLTO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved sinterability.

title: Aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by sputtering followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 100 nm. The LiF material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the cycle life of the lithium metal battery.

title: Hafnium-substituted perovskite-type LLTO solid electrolyte stable above 4.5 V and method for preparing the same
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte stable against oxidation above 4.5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more and a conductivity of 0.35 mS/cm or more. The positive electrode active material is LiCoPO4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The hafnium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability in contact with lithium.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer comprises ceramic ion conductor particles, a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li2ZrO3, LATP, and LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The binder is styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent butyl butyrate. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The solid content is 40 wt% to 60 wt%, the viscosity is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the ceramic ion conductor, and the layer shows improved sinterability.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which ceramic ion conductor particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The sheet thickness is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers, the porosity is 30% or less, and the conductivity is 1.4 mS/cm or more. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A solid-state lithium battery using the sheet shows improved cycle life and a thinner electrolyte layer.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X solid electrolyte having anion disorder and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X solid electrolyte in which part of the bromine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 5.1 mS/cm. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life of the all-solid-state lithium battery.
